=== GroupTrack_V24_WorkPlan_Apr29.docx ===




GroupTrack V2.4
Wednesday April 29, 2026
Work Plan � Problem Definitions & Repair Strategies

Goal: Complete all fixes, rebuild AAB, publish to Google Play Store

Prepared: April 28, 2026 � Confidential


Task Schedule Overview
All tasks are sequenced by priority. Track display reliability is the gating issue � all other work depends on a working track pipeline. Google Play submission closes the day.


Total estimated time: approximately 4.5 hours

Task 1: Remove 0.25mi Segment Jump Rejection
Problem Definition
ConvoyViewModel.kt contains a distance filter that rejects any track segment longer than 0.25 miles. When a radio drops and reconnects, the lead cart has moved beyond this threshold. The reconnection segment is silently discarded with a log message "LEAD SEGMENT JUMP REJECTED". This creates visible gaps in the track display.
The filter exists on two code paths:
Lead-only track: line 593 � if (segDist > 0.25f) { ... rejected }
Multi-cart track: line 617 � identical filter for all carts
Field test evidence: 5 radios covering 14 carts with long distance gaps between radios. Every radio dropout exceeding 0.25 miles of travel created a permanent gap in the displayed track.

Repair Strategy
Delete the distance check and rejection block at line 593 (lead track path)
Delete the distance check and rejection block at line 617 (multi-cart path)
Always create the segment regardless of distance
Keep the convoyLog for debugging but remove the skip logic

Design principle: Every segment draws, always. No exceptions. Angular lines through curves will be smoothed in V2.5. First priority is a complete, continuous track.

Files Modified
ConvoyViewModel.kt � lines 590-596 (lead path), lines 614-618 (multi path)

Task 2: Cart Position Substitution for Silent Carts
Problem Definition
When a cart drops from the node list (radio disconnect, out of range, interference), the tick() function in ConvoyViewModel.kt stops accumulating trail segments for that cart. The track display freezes at the last known position and no new segments are drawn until the cart reappears.
Current code at line 577-578:
val leadNode = if (_leadLockedFlag) state.lead else null
if (leadNode != null) { ... }  // null on disconnect = nothing draws
When state.lead is null, the entire trail accumulation block is skipped. The track goes dead.

Field test evidence: Lead cart track stopped recording/displaying whenever the radio dropped. With 5 radios spread across 14 carts and long distances, this happened frequently. Tracks were always broken despite continuous GPS availability on the device.

Repair Strategy
Universal rule for ALL carts, not just the lead:
If a cart is not reporting, set its position to whichever is further along: its own last known position OR the furthest active cart behind it.

Implementation steps:
When state.lead is null but lockedLeadNodeId is set, do not skip the trail block
Use lastLeadLat / lastLeadLon as the current anchor (already tracked)
Check other active carts in the node list � find any cart whose position is further along than the lead's last known position
"Further along" = greater haversine distance from the first trackpoint, or simply further in the direction of travel
If an active cart is beyond the lead's last position, substitute that cart's position as the new trackpoint for the trail line
When lead cart reappears in the node list, resume using its actual position � draw connecting segment regardless of distance (Task 1 already ensures this)
Apply the same logic to the multi-cart path (line 607+) for all carts in the convoy

Key constraints:
Lead assignment NEVER changes � lead stays locked to cart 1 always
Only the position source temporarily falls back to nearest active cart
Track lines never go backwards � substituted position must be further along than last known
The tick engine already tracks all cart positions � data is available, just not being used for trail building

Files Modified
ConvoyViewModel.kt � tick() function, lines 575-635

Task 3: Test Track Display with Radio Disconnect
Test Plan
Build debug APK with Tasks 1-2 applied
Install on Android 1: adb -s 8624SBCEDF00001789 install -r -d [apk]
Start track recording with radio connected
Verify track draws continuously while driving
Power off the T1000-E radio mid-ride
Continue driving � verify track continues drawing using GPS/substituted position
Power radio back on � verify track connects through with no gap
Stop recording � verify GPX file has continuous trackpoints throughout
Check convoy log for any JUMP REJECTED messages (should be zero)

Success criteria: Continuous track line from start to finish with zero gaps, regardless of radio state changes.

Task 4: Auto-Pause GPS Recording
Problem Definition
The GPS LocationListener has a 5-meter minimum distance filter. When stationary (lunch stop, staging area), no positions fire and no trackpoints are written. This creates time gaps in the GPX file. The April 27 field test showed a 1 hour 23 minute gap at a lunch stop � the recording was running but no points were being written.
Users also restart recording to reassign the lead cart or recover from a perceived issue, creating multiple short GPX files that must be manually stitched together to reconstruct a full day's route.

Repair Strategy
Track the timestamp of the last GPS position received in ConvoyGpsService
On each LocationListener callback, check elapsed time since last position
If no position change for 60 seconds (1 minute), log auto-pause but keep the GPX file open
When the next position arrives after the pause, auto-resume � write the new trackpoint directly
The GPX file draws a straight line from the pause point to the resume point � this is correct behavior (lunch stop to departure)
No new temp file is created � single continuous GPX per session

The auto-pause is transparent to the user. Recording indicator stays active. No stop/start cycle needed.

Files Modified
ConvoyGpsService.kt � LocationListener callback (~line 244), add lastPositionTimestamp tracking

Task 5: GPX Combine � Select Multiple Tracks, Merge as One
Problem Definition
Field testing required multiple stop/start recording cycles during a single day. The April 26 route produced 2 separate GPX files (abc and bar_10) that together represent the complete route. Currently there is no way to select multiple tracks and combine them into a single GPX file for sharing or analysis.
April 27 had similar fragmentation � the full day's route was split across multiple recordings due to app restarts and lead cart reassignment.

Repair Strategy
In the track picker list, allow multi-select mode (checkboxes instead of single-tap load)
Add a COMBINE button next to ALL / FIT / CLEAR
When COMBINE is tapped, read all selected GPX files
Sort trackpoints by timestamp across all files
Write a new combined GPX file with all trackpoints in chronological order as a single <trkseg>
Prompt user for a file name for the combined track
Save to my_tracks directory and refresh the list

Date grouping enhancement: Add a date filter next to the existing controls. Tap a date to show only tracks from that day. Makes it easy to select all recordings from a field test day and combine them.

Files Modified
ConvoyScreen.kt � track picker UI (~line 1040+), add multi-select and COMBINE button
ConvoyScreen.kt � new function convoyMergeTracks() for GPX combining

Task 6: Debug Track List Slow Opening
Problem Definition
Tapping the TRACKS button shows "0 of 0" for 30-60 seconds before displaying the file list. The directory contains 31 files (10 displayed after filtering). The listing function (convoyListTracks) runs on Dispatchers.IO and only reads file names � it does not parse file contents. Despite this, the display is severely delayed.
Observations:
GeoJSON trails are already loaded and displayed before TRACKS is tapped � IO dispatcher is not competing with GeoJSON loading
One trashed file in the directory is 31MB � filesystem stat on this file may contribute
450,000 tile files at z18 may cause filesystem inode pressure affecting all IO operations
Individual track loading after selection is fast � only the initial name listing is slow

Repair Strategy
Add timing logs to convoyListTracks: log timestamp before and after listFiles(), filter, sort
Add timing log around the MainScope launch and withContext callback
Run app and tap TRACKS � check logcat for exact timing of each operation
If listFiles() is fast but UI update is delayed � issue is Compose recomposition or main thread blocking
If listFiles() is slow � issue is filesystem pressure from tile directories; consider caching the file list
Clean up trashed/temp files to reduce directory enumeration load

Diagnostic Commands
adb -s 8624SBCEDF00001789 logcat -v time | grep -i "convoyListTracks\|track.*list\|track.*time"

Task 7: Debug ANR "Cancel or Wait" on App Open
Problem Definition
The app displays an Application Not Responding dialog ("Cancel or Wait") on startup. This occurs before any radio is connected. It happens even after a device reboot. Tapping Cancel force-kills the app, which can interrupt any active GPS recording session (foreground service dies with the app process).
The ANR dialog appears when the main (UI) thread is blocked for more than 5 seconds. Something during app initialization is performing heavy work on the main thread.

Likely candidates:
GeoJSON trail overlay loading � 5,724 features across 8 Utah counties parsed from bundled assets
SharedPreferences initialization or migration logic
WebView initialization (Chromium cold start)
Tile directory enumeration on first map render
MeshService binding and initialization

Repair Strategy
Clear logcat, launch app fresh, capture ANR trace:
adb -s 8624SBCEDF00001789 logcat -c
# Launch app, wait for ANR dialog
adb -s 8624SBCEDF00001789 logcat -d | grep -iE "ANR in|Input dispatching|Slow|BlockMonitor" | head -20

Pull the ANR traces file for detailed stack trace:
adb -s 8624SBCEDF00001789 shell cat /data/anr/traces.txt | head -100

The stack trace will show exactly which method is blocking the main thread
Move the blocking operation to a coroutine on Dispatchers.IO or a background Thread
If it is GeoJSON loading: move to background thread, show map without trails, add trails once loaded
If it is WebView init: already unavoidable on first launch, consider splash screen to mask it

Files Modified
TBD � depends on diagnostic results. Likely ConvoyScreen.kt or MainActivity.kt

Task 8: Show Downloads Performance Fixes
Problem Definition
The Show Downloaded Areas button triggers a filesystem scan to determine the bounding rectangle of downloaded tile regions. The scan uses listFiles() recursively through tile directories.
ConvoyScreen.kt line 512 scans zoom level 18, which contains approximately 450,000 tile entries. This takes 4+ minutes. Lines 1243 (ConvoyScreen) and 472 (MapViewerScreen) already use z14 (76 directories, 1-2 seconds).
Additional issues: no loading feedback, button can be tapped multiple times stacking scan threads, no way to cancel a running scan.

Repair Strategy
Four sub-fixes:
Change z18 to z14 at line 512 and update tile path to "SAT/14" � reduces scan from 450K entries to 76 directories
Add a loading spinner (CircularProgressIndicator) visible while scan thread is running
Disable the button (or set a flag to ignore taps) while scan is in progress
Store the scan Thread reference; before starting a new scan, interrupt the existing one and check an isScanning flag inside the forEach loop to bail out early

Files Modified
ConvoyScreen.kt � line 512 (z level + path), line ~510 (spinner state), line ~508 (button disable)

Tasks 9-11: Build, Publish, and Verify
Task 9: Rebuild AAB
After all fixes are applied and tested:
Commit all changes: git add -A && git commit -m "V2.4 field test fixes"
Build release AAB:
./gradlew bundleGoogleRelease -x uploadCrashlyticsMappingFileGoogleRelease
Copy to Downloads:
cp app/build/outputs/bundle/googleRelease/app-google-release.aab "/c/Users/kixaz/Downloads/GroupTrack_v2.4_final.aab"

Task 10: Play Store Submission
Open https://play.google.com/console
Click GroupTrack app

=== GroupTrack_V25_Backlog.docx ===
GroupTrack V2.5 � Backlog and Task Planning
Captured 2026-05-07. Carry forward into V2.5 development planning.
Purpose
V2.5 follows the V2.4 Play Store release. The strategic goal is twofold: (1) build out the standalone product (no-radio, solo-rider) to full feature parity with Gaia GPS and onX, expanding GroupTrack's audience to riders who don't yet own a Meshtastic radio; (2) lay the architectural foundation for national trail coverage and cloud-synced tile/track distribution. V2.5 is the bridge from "convoy-tracking app for radio owners" to "free GPS tracker for any rider, with convoy capability when a radio is added."
Items below are organized by theme. Priorities for the V2.5 release scope are flagged. Architecture-level work is the longest-running.
Architecture � National Trail Model
Replaces the current 22 MB Utah GeoJSON with a unified GeoPackage architecture and three engines that handle ingestion, distribution, and local display.
Components
Unified GeoPackage file: grouptrack.gpkg, replaces the 22 MB Utah GeoJSON entirely.
Ingestion engine: pulls from authoritative sources (UGRC, BLM, USFS, etc.) on a per-region basis. Outputs into the GeoPackage.
Distribution engine: serves regions to clients. Region-based downloads paired with the same region's tile set.
Local display engine: efficient query and render of GeoPackage data on Android. Replaces current GeoJSON loader.
Rollout plan
Utah pilot first � replaces existing 5,732-trail Utah GeoJSON with GeoPackage equivalent. Validates the pipeline end-to-end.
Expand to neighboring states (AZ, NV, ID, CO) once Utah is stable.
National coverage as Phase 3 of V2.5.
This is the longest single piece of V2.5 work. Multiple weeks, not days.
Track Display Selector � Filter Tabs and In-Progress Files
Captured tonight: extend the track display selector on ConvoyScreen.kt and ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt (the on/off toggle for track overlays on the map) to include in-progress files alongside saved tracks.
Filter tabs: All / Saved / In-Progress (mirroring the Work With Tracks pattern).
Reuses ConvoyTrackOps.isInProgress() predicate that already exists. No new file ops logic.
In-progress files become selectable AND renameable from the selector � solves the "the only way to rename unsaved files is to display them" problem.
UI work only. Backend already complete.
Track Import � Move to Map Viewer
V2.4 will ship with track import in the convoy map's MAP SETTINGS submenu (alongside Export). V2.5 moves it to the Map Viewer settings menu, aligning with the broader V2.5 architecture: Map Viewer becomes the hub for ALL track management � display, import, export, email, file management.
Remove "Import Tracks from Downloads" from ConvoySubMenu.kt MAP SETTINGS
Add to Map Viewer settings menu
Same composable, different menu placement. Small refactor.
Standalone Product Polish � Gaia/onX Feature Parity
V2.4 introduces standalone mode functionally. V2.5 polishes it to feel like a finished product for the solo rider.
Higher-resolution GPS recording � 1-second interval option (currently fixed at 3s)
Mileage / trip odometer display � referenced in V2.4 known limitations as "planned for future"
Speed warmup tightening � currently shows 0 mph for ~60 seconds while GPS samples accumulate
Track stats display � distance, elevation gain, moving time, max speed (post-ride summary)
Waypoint marking on the map (POIs along a ride)
Solo rider onboarding flow � first-launch tutorial that doesn't assume a radio
Marketing copy on splash / about screen positioning the app as standalone-friendly
Map Manager Phase C
Substantial map system work captured in earlier sessions. Listed here for completeness; full design exists in earlier docs.


=== GroupTrack_V25_ConsolidatedDesign_May17_v2.docx ===
GroupTrack V2.5 � Consolidated Design Document
May 17, 2026 � Version 2
Timeline: 4 weeks � all 7 tasks ship together
Approach: Phase 0 scaffolding first, then features hang on scaffolding
Design all UI and rules before any coding. No refactoring.
Implementation Boundaries
Clear boundaries between V2.5 and V2.6 prevent rabbit holes. Build collection mechanisms now, wire processing later.
V2.5 scope (4 weeks)
Phase 0: Complete UI scaffolding with all placeholders and navigation changes
Task 1: Source picker � fully functional
Task 2: Tile queue enhancements � new job types, priority, remove area
Task 3: Spatial trails � area-bounded agency import, viewport lazy-load
Task 4: Spatial tracks � spatial index, alias model, area filtering
Task 5: Waypoints � long-press creation, 10 types, area display
Task 6: Routes � point-to-point draw, snap-to-trail, type flip from track
Task 7: Upload queue infrastructure BUILT, share prompt COLLECTING, queue NOT PROCESSING
Task 7: Download functions are STUBS only
Task 7: No AWS backend integration � no network upload code
Server browse UI is paygated STUB
V2.6 scope (future)
Task 7: Upload queue processing ACTIVATED � items accumulated in V2.5 start uploading
Task 7: Download functions WIRED � area search, browse, select, download
Task 7: AWS backend integration � spatial data API endpoints
Server browse UI functional behind paygate
Ride enrollment download triggers
CV-assisted route path smoothing
Boundary rules
V2.5 upload queue collects items locally. Does not send to AWS.
V2.5 share prompt works and populates queue table. No network calls.
V2.5 download menu sections exist as stubs. Not wired to AWS.
V2.5 server browse UI shows paygate prompt. No server queries.
V2.6 flips the switch � processing code added, queue starts sending.
Never build processing code during V2.5. Only collection and UI.

Architecture Overview
Development phases
Phase 0: Scaffolding � all placeholder screens, navigation changes, stub menus, shared components
Phase 1: Infrastructure � Task 1 (Source Picker) + Task 2 (Tile Queue enhancements)
Phase 2: Spatial Engine � Task 3 (Trails) + Task 4 (Tracks). Patterns set here reuse in Phase 3.
Phase 3: User Data � Task 5 (Waypoints) + Task 6 (Routes). Creation tools on Planning Map.
Phase 4: Integration � Task 7 (Area Data Transfer collection) + convoy map cutover.
Two separate queues
Tile queue (Task 2): downloads, refreshes, removes map tiles. Tiles follow spatial data automatically. Never uploads tiles.
Spatial data queue (Task 7): collects items for upload via share prompt. Queue built in V2.5, processing activated in V2.6.
Two data sources
Local (default, always shown, free): all local spatial data. Create, edit, collect for upload.
Server (enhanced, paygated): browse shared data from AWS. V2.5 = stub. V2.6 = functional.
Source selector toggle between Local/Server � never mixed on same display.
Data flow rules
Uploads are per-item, triggered by share prompt on save. Never area-based.
Uploads are spatial data only � no tiles ever uploaded to AWS.
V2.5 uploads collect to local queue only. No network transmission.
Downloads use area search for discovery, item selection for download, area-inclusive for associated data.
An area on the server is a collection of tracks, routes, and waypoints (one or many).
Downloaded spatial data auto-generates tile download requests from item geometry.
Tiles are never downloaded in isolation � always follow spatial data.
High priority tiles when explicit track/route downloaded. Low priority for area-based spatial downloads.
Tile refreshes only as byproduct of spatial data downloads. Never standalone.
Manual area draw (existing) stays for initial tile downloads.
All operations user-initiated. No operations on launch. No auto-sync.
Tiles never transit AWS. Always sourced from tile providers (Esri, Google, etc.).
Shared components (built in Phase 0)
Area selector � reusable across all spatial data tasks
Source selector (Local/Server toggle) � reusable across Tasks 4, 5, 6
Share prompt dialog � reusable on every save action, populates upload queue
Paygate prompt � checks subscription status, shows upgrade prompt

Task 1: Source Picker
Objective
Expose 16 built-in map sources from map_sources.json to user selection. Users assign any source to any of 3 map slots. Map Viewer only � convoy map stays on defaults until cutover.
UI elements
One "Change Map Source" button added to display menu

=== GroupTrack_V25_DecisionLog_May17.docx ===
GroupTrack V2.5 -- Complete Decision Log
Extracted from May 17, 2026 full-day session
GREEN = Decision made | ORANGE = Open issue requiring resolution
1. ANR Fixes (Completed)
1.1 WorkManager ANR
MeshLogCleanupWorker: Changed ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE to KEEP -- prevents re-trigger on every cold start
Added 30-second initial delay to PeriodicWorkRequest -- first run doesn't compete with startup
Added WorkManager.pruneWork() before scheduleMeshLogCleanup() -- clears stale finished jobs
File: MeshUtilApplication.kt -- committed and deployed
1.2 MediaStore ANR (Root Cause)
scanImportDirectory() contained legacy MediaStore.Downloads query for .convoy files
This query blocked main thread via ContentResolver.query() Binder IPC when Media Provider was busy indexing tile files
Confirmed via bugreport thread dump: main thread stuck in ContentProviderProxy.query() inside ConvoyViewModel init
Fix: Removed the MediaStore.Downloads query entirely -- ConvoyFileReceiver handles .convoy imports via intents now
scanImportDirectory() retained for processing files in convoy_import/ directory
Dispatchers.IO added to scanImportDirectory launch as belt-and-suspenders
File: ConvoyViewModel.kt -- committed and deployed
NO MediaStore queries anywhere in the app. This is a standing rule.
1.3 P10_T Device Findings
P10_T advertises 4GB RAM but kernel sees only 2.9GB (Unisoc/Spreadtrum chipset reserves ~1.1GB)
P10_T is NOT incompatible hardware -- same build loads in 1 second after MediaStore fix
Tester had ~60GB of tiles in Downloads, causing Media Provider to run at 58% CPU
Google Media Provider indexing large tile directories makes ALL ContentResolver queries slow via Binder IPC
Factory reset fixes were misleading -- it was the MediaStore query + busy Media Provider, not accumulated state
ServiceKeepAliveWorker lint warning: missing connectedDevice foregroundServiceType in AndroidManifest.xml -- needs fix

2. Device Assignments
Android 1 (P50, 8624SBCEDF00001789): Release APK only. Acceptance test device.
Android 2 (EP103B, 24039703201775): Play Store release for field testing. V3.0 debug deferred until V2.5 complete.
P10_T (P10V07162601000362): Play Store release. ANR fixed. 3GB usable RAM but functional.
Debug APK never on Android 1. Release APK never on Android 2. Play Store only on P10_T.
Play Store and local APK use different signing keys -- must uninstall one before installing the other.
Never mix debug/release on a device. Leaves stale signing artifacts.

3. V2.5 Architecture Decisions
3.1 Development Approach
Phase 0 scaffolding ships first -- ALL UI placeholders before any feature code
4-week timeline, all 7 tasks ship together
Scaffolding-first: build the skeleton, hang features on it. No refactoring.
Design all UI and rules before any coding. HTML panel mockups as reference.
Each feature: PLAN, RESEARCH (xref), AGREE, BUILD
One comprehensive patch per agreed design, not piecemeal changes
3.2  Separate Queues
Tile queue (Task 2): downloads, refreshes, removes map tiles. Never uploads.
Spatial data queue (Task 7): collects uploads via share prompt. Separate from tile queue.
3.3 Two Data Sources
LOCAL: default, always shown, free. All local spatial data.
SERVER: enhanced, paygated ($3/month). Browse shared data from AWS.

3.4 Upload Rules

V2.5: upload queue COLLECTS only. No processing, no network transmission.
V2.6: processing activated, accumulated items start uploading.

3.5 Download Rules
Downloads use area for DISCOVERY -- find what's available on server.
User selects SPECIFIC items (one or many tracks/routes) to download.
Download is AREA-INCLUSIVE -- selected item + associated waypoints within coverage.
An area on the server is a COLLECTION of tracks, routes, and waypoints (one or many).
Downloaded spatial data AUTO-GENERATES tile download requests from item geometry.
Downloads are STUB only in V2.5. Functional in V2.6.
3.6 Tile Rules
Tiles are NEVER by the user.
Tiles ALWAYS ollow spatial data .
HIGH priority tiles when explicit track/route downloaded.
LOW priority tiles when area-based spatial data downloaded.
Tile refreshes NEVER standalone -- only as byproduct of spatial data download.
Tile coverage maps to route + track + waypoint GEOMETRY within area, NOT full bbox.
Manual area draw (existing) stays for initial tile downloads.
Two methods for initial tile download: manual area draw (broad) or spatial data request (targeted along geometry).
Remove area tiles is the ONLY explicit user tile action (storage management).
Tiles NEVER transit AWS. Always sourced from tile providers (Esri, Google, etc.).

Offline-first. Every feature works without connectivity.
Canvas independence. Map tiles are the user's choice.
Cumulative collection. Downloads add data. Only explicit removal deletes.
Routes never independently public. Only through ride invitations.
Private rides block sharing. Toggle suppresses share prompt entirely.
Published content always recoverable from collective (V3.0).
Trails and routes never removed individually. Source/region removal only.
First source ingested wins auto-resolve for duplicates.
Reusability: Ops files (logic) and Dialogs files (UI).
Every user data change is journaled. No exceptions.
Backup before every destructive operation. Automatic.
Journal stores before AND after state with geometry as WKT.
Schema must be hardened before application code.
Lifecycle triggers designed and tested before features built.
Patch scripts uniquely versioned Python files. Never reuse names.
Never commit V3_FEATURES_ENABLED or V25_SPATIAL_ENABLED = true.
Preserve full trail geometry precision.
Complete impact analysis before ANY code change.
All imports are tracks. Always. Convert to route is explicit type flip.
Track and route share same table with type field.
Tiles are never downloaded in isolation. Always follow spatial data.
Tile coverage maps to spatial data geometry, not full bbox.

Uploads are spatial data only. Tiles never transit AWS.
V2.5 upload queue collects only. No processing.
Downloads use area for discovery, item selection for download.
Server browsing and downloads are paygated.
Local and server data never mixed on same display.
All operations user-initiated. No operations on launch. No auto-sync.
No MediaStore queries. Lesson from P10_T ANR.

1. ANR Fixes (Completed)
1.1 WorkManager ANR
MeshLogCleanupWorker: Changed ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE to KEEP -- prevents re-trigger on every cold start
Added 30-second initial delay to PeriodicWorkRequest -- first run doesn't compete with startup
Added WorkManager.pruneWork() before scheduleMeshLogCleanup() -- clears stale finished jobs
File: MeshUtilApplication.kt -- committed and deployed
1.2 MediaStore ANR (Root Cause)
scanImportDirectory() contained legacy MediaStore.Downloads query for .convoy files
This query blocked main thread via ContentResolver.query() Binder IPC when Media Provider was busy indexing tile files
Confirmed via bugreport thread dump: main thread stuck in ContentProviderProxy.query() inside ConvoyViewModel init
Fix: Removed the MediaStore.Downloads query entirely -- ConvoyFileReceiver handles .convoy imports via intents now
scanImportDirectory() retained for processing files in convoy_import/ directory
Dispatchers.IO added to scanImportDirectory launch as belt-and-suspenders
File: ConvoyViewModel.kt -- committed and deployed
NO MediaStore queries anywhere in the app. This is a standing rule.
1.3 P10_T Device Findings
P10_T advertises 4GB RAM but kernel sees only 2.9GB (Unisoc/Spreadtrum chipset reserves ~1.1GB)
P10_T is NOT incompatible hardware -- same build loads in 1 second after MediaStore fix
Tester had ~60GB of tiles in Downloads, causing Media Provider to run at 58% CPU
Google Media Provider indexing large tile directories makes ALL ContentResolver queries slow via Binder IPC
Factory reset fixes were misleading -- it was the MediaStore query + busy Media Provider, not accumulated state
ServiceKeepAliveWorker lint warning: missing connectedDevice foregroundServiceType in AndroidManifest.xml -- needs fix

Android 1 (P50, 8624SBCEDF00001789): Release APK only. Acceptance test device.
Android 2 (EP103B, 24039703201775): Play Store release for field testing. V3.0 debug deferred until V2.5 complete.
P10_T (P10V07162601000362): Play Store release. ANR fixed. 3GB usable RAM but functional.
Debug APK never on Android 1. Release APK never on Android 2. Play Store only on P10_T.
Play Store and local APK use different signing keys -- must uninstall one before installing the other.
Never mix debug/release on a device. Leaves stale signing artifacts.

Spatial queues (upload and download) NOT active exchanges with AWS until V2.6.

LOCAL: default, always shown, free. All local spatial data.

3.5 Download Rules (V2.6 Feature)
Downloads use area for DISCOVERY -- find what's available on server.
User selects SPECIFIC items (one or many tracks/routes) to download.

Downloaded spatial data AUTO-GENERATES tile download requests from item geometry.
Downloads are STUB only in V2.5. Functional in V2.6.
3.6 Tile Rules
Tiles are NEVER refreshed by area or downloaded in isolation by the user.
Tiles ALWAYS refresh following spatial data creation (trigger-based) automatically.
HIGH priority tiles when explicit track/route are downloaded. V2.5: import of tracks only or route creation based on triggers.
LOW priority tiles when area-based spatial data downloaded. V2.5: import of trail sources.
Tile refreshes NEVER standalone -- only as byproduct of spatial data creation or download.
Tile coverage maps to route + track + waypoint GEOMETRY within area, NOT full bbox.
Manual area draw (existing) stays for initial tile downloads.

Remove area tiles is the ONLY explicit user tile action on stored tiles (storage management).
Tiles NEVER transit AWS. Always sourced from tile providers (Esri, Google, etc.).
Work with Queues displays status and details across all three queues.
Existing queue panel filtered by priority. Job type IS priority.
Tile refreshes happen when spatial data is CREATED in V2.5 or DOWNLOADED in V2.6.
Trail imports refresh downloaded tiles only. Routes and tracks refresh AND create tiles. All trigger-based.
3.7 Area Concept
Area selector is a TRANSIENT definition that is NOT saved. Shared component across all spatial data tasks.
Areas are independent of rides -- rides are just one method to request area spatial data.
Area used for: trail download boundaries, tile download targeting, spatial data discovery.
Tile areas mapped to route/track/waypoint GEOMETRY to minimize downloaded data.
Download spatial data auto-creates tile download request for supporting tiles.
3.8 Spatial Data Creation
Trails: imported from external agency sources only. Never created in-app. Import process adds to spatial db.
Tracks: primarily created through app processes via triggers (GPS recording). GPX/KML import from Downloads is secondary path.
Routes: created through app processes via triggers (draw, snap, convert). Import enters as track first.
Waypoints: created through app processes via triggers (long-press). Import from external files is secondary path.
Triggers are the main method for non-trail data. Import vs create-in-process -- different method, same outcome: spatial db entry.

3. V2.5 Architecture
3.1 Core UI Architecture
TWO BUTTONS, TWO ACCORDION BARS. Everything launches from there, closes to nothing when done.
Work with Artifacts: button on Display bar. Accordion with per-type rows. DISPLAY/EDIT/IMPORT (Planning). DISPLAY only (Convoy).
Work with Queues: button upper right of map. Replaces track button on Planning Map. Summary dropdown + twisty drill-down.
Minimal real estate. Open = compact accordion. Function launched = focused panel. Done = zero footprint.
Consistent display format between Convoy and Planning maps. Convoy blocks some functions but same visual.
Standardized artifact detail panel. Same layout for all types. Type-specific actions vary.
3.2 THREE Separate Queues
Upload spatial queue: collects items via share prompt. V2.5 collect only. V2.6 processes.
Download spatial queue: downloads tracks, routes, waypoints from AWS. V2.6 feature.
Download tiles queue: downloads, refreshes, removes map tiles. Always active.
Spatial queues NOT active with AWS until V2.6.
Three queues never mixed. Different job types, different managers, different priorities.
3.3 Two Data Sources
LOCAL: default, free. SERVER: paygated ($3/month). Planning Map only. Never mixed on same display.
Source selector is V2.6 feature. V2.5: paygated stub only.
3.4 Upload Rules
Uploads are PER-ITEM via share prompt on save. Routes and tracks inclusive of waypoints.
Uploads are NEVER area-based. No bulk upload. No upload button.
Share prompt: simple toggle 'Share this artifact with other GroupTrack users? Yes/No'
Share prompt controlled by app_setting and ride privacy toggle. Private ride suppresses entirely.
V2.5: collect only. V2.6: processing activated. No downloads until uploads started processing.
Never build V2.6 processing code during V2.5.
3.5 Download Rules (V2.6 Feature)
Downloads use area for discovery. User selects specific items. Download is area-inclusive with associated waypoints.
Downloaded spatial data auto-generates tile download requests from geometry.
3.6 Download Panel Structure
V2.5 ACTIVE: Download Tiles (manual area draw), Delete Area Tiles (storage management).
V2.6 STUBS: Download Area (spatial by area), Download Artifact (specific item), Upload Artifacts (process queue).
V2.6 buttons show paygate or 'coming soon' when tapped in V2.5.
3.7 Tile Rules
Tiles NEVER refreshed by area or downloaded in isolation by user.
Tiles ALWAYS refresh following spatial data creation (trigger-based).
HIGH priority: explicit track/route creation. V2.5: track import or route creation triggers.
LOW priority: area-based trail import.
MED priority: source refresh after map source change.
Trail imports refresh downloaded tiles only. Routes and tracks refresh AND create tiles.
Remove area tiles is the ONLY explicit user tile action on stored tiles.
Manual area draw stays for initial tile downloads.
Tiles NEVER transit AWS. Always from tile providers.
All tile operations are trigger-based. Never user-initiated except manual area draw and remove.
3.8 Area Concept
Area selector is TRANSIENT -- not saved. Shared component.
Areas independent of rides. Rides are just one method to request area spatial data.
3.9 Spatial Data Creation
Triggers are the main method for non-trail data creation.
Tracks: GPS recording creates trigger. Save + name prompt at end of recording. Share prompt follows.
Waypoints: long-press on BOTH maps creates trigger. 10 types, name entry, proximity 100m.
Routes: draw/snap/convert creates trigger.
Trails: imported from vetted/approved external sources only. Never created in-app.
Import is for external sources only. Creation via triggers is the primary path.
3.10 Data Model
Tracks: source of truth = GPX/KML file. SQL holds metadata + bbox as index via triggers.
Waypoints: SQL tables only. No backing file. DB is source of truth.
Routes: SQL tables only (TBD -- if existing schema supports location, may use trigger route like tracks).
Trails: SQL tables only after import. Source file not retained.
Route schema to be researched during Task 6 build. No impact on screen design.
Upload queue mirrors download queue design. Push instead of pull. Same states and priorities.

=== GroupTrack_V25_LifecycleOwnership.docx ===
GroupTrack V2.5
Lifecycle Ownership + Data Integrity
May 18, 2026 | All sessions incorporated
1. Entity Ownership Map
Each Kotlin entity owns a specific artifact lifecycle. No shared ownership. No ambiguity about who does what.
2. Lifecycle Chains
Every creation, update, and deletion follows a defined chain. No step is optional. No dangling records.
2.1 Trail Import
Trigger: User initiates import via Work with Artifacts > Trails > IMPORT
Owner: TrailImporter
Parse source file (GeoJSON/Shapefile) per trail_sources catalog format
For each trail feature: check source_unique_id against existing trails
IF EXISTS: AliasManager adds PrimaryName as new alias. No new spatial record.
IF NEW: Insert trails (spatial). Insert trail_properties (extension). AliasManager inserts first alias (preferred, source='agency').
AuditLogger: data_log entry (action='import')
TileRequestTrigger: tile_queue entry (LOW priority, trail geometry extent)
Update source_ingestions with count, dupes skipped, filters used
2.2 Track Creation (GPS Recording)
Trigger: GPS recording stops
Owner: TrackManager
Prompt: name the track
Save or Skip. Skip = discard file and exit.
Save GPX/KML file to Documents/my_tracks/
Insert tracks (spatial, bbox computed from file)
Insert track_properties (distance, duration, speed, elevation from file)
AliasManager: insert alias (preferred, source='user')
Prompt: 'Available to all riders? Y/N' � if Y, set shared=1
Survey: enjoyment 1-5, ride again Y/N � insert track_surveys
AuditLogger: data_log entry (action='create')
If shared: QueueManager inserts upload_queue entry
TileRequestTrigger: tile_queue entry (HIGH priority)
2.3 Track Creation (File Import)
Trigger: User selects GPX/KML via Work with Artifacts > Tracks > IMPORT
Owner: TrackManager
Same as GPS recording steps 3�11, except file is copied from Downloads to my_tracks/ instead of created by GPS.
2.4 Waypoint Creation (Long-Press)
Trigger: Long-press on map (both Convoy and Planning maps)
Owner: WaypointManager
User selects waypoint type from grid (10 types)
Proximity check: query waypoints within 100m of press location
IF NEARBY FOUND: show existing waypoints with all aliases. User chooses: (A) Add alias to existing, (B) Select preferred on existing, (C) Create new anyway.
IF (A): AliasManager adds alias to existing waypoint. No new spatial record. Done.
IF (B): AliasManager sets preferred on existing. Done.
IF (C) or NO NEARBY: prompt for name
Insert waypoints (spatial, point geometry from press location)
Insert waypoint_properties (elevation from GPS)
AliasManager: insert alias (preferred, source='user')
AuditLogger: data_log entry (action='create')
Share prompt: Y/N � if Y, shared=1, QueueManager inserts upload_queue
2.5 Route Creation
Trigger: User initiates via draw/snap-to-trail/convert-from-track
Owner: RouteManager
User creates route geometry (draw, snap, or convert)
Prompt: name the route
Insert routes (spatial, linestring geometry)
Insert route_properties (distance, method, source_track_id if converted, trailhead_id=null)
AliasManager: insert alias (preferred, source='user')
AuditLogger: data_log entry (action='create')
TileRequestTrigger: tile_queue entry (HIGH priority)
RULE: trailhead_id nullable at creation. Required before ride release (V2.6). Rides = V3.0.
V2.6: Route creation should check AWS for existing tracks in area and present alias names for reference.
3. Delete Chains
3.1 Delete Trail
Owner: TrailImporter (trails removed by source/region batch, never individually)
Cascade: trail_properties deleted (Kotlin trigger)
Cascade: artifact_aliases where type='trail' deleted (Kotlin trigger)
AuditLogger: data_log entry (action='delete', before_state=snapshot)
No upload_queue impact (trails are agency data, not user shared)
3.2 Delete Track
Owner: TrackManager
Check: route_properties.source_track_id references this track?
If yes: warn user, allow force delete (nullifies source_track_id)
Cascade: track_properties deleted
Cascade: track_surveys deleted
Cascade: artifact_aliases where type='track' deleted
Remove from upload_queue if queued
AuditLogger: data_log entry (action='delete')
File in my_tracks/ optionally deleted (user choice)
3.3 Delete Waypoint
Owner: WaypointManager
Check: route_properties.trailhead_id references this waypoint?
If yes: BLOCK delete. User must reassign trailhead on route first.
Cascade: waypoint_properties deleted
Cascade: artifact_aliases where type='waypoint' deleted
Remove from upload_queue if queued
AuditLogger: data_log entry (action='delete')
3.4 Delete Route
Owner: RouteManager
Check: route_properties.ride_id is not null?
If yes: BLOCK delete. Route assigned to ride. Must remove from ride first.
Cascade: route_properties deleted
Cascade: artifact_aliases where type='route' deleted
AuditLogger: data_log entry (action='delete')
4. Alias Lifecycle
Owner: AliasManager (all alias operations, all artifact types)
4.1 Alias Integrity Rules
Every artifact must have at least one alias at all times
Exactly one alias has is_preferred=1 per artifact (enforced by AliasManager)
Agency aliases (source='agency') cannot be deleted by user
AWS aliases (source='aws') cannot be deleted by user
User aliases (source='user') can be deleted, unless it is the only alias
On delete preferred: auto-promote next alias (agency first, then aws, then oldest user)
is_preferred is LOCAL ONLY. Not sent to AWS. Each user picks their own display.
4.2 Alias Display Chain
Display name = COALESCE(preferred_alias, spatial.name, agency_id, 'Unnamed')
v_preferred_aliases view returns one preferred alias per artifact
v_trail_display, v_track_display views join spatial + alias + properties for display
4.3 Alias in Data Exchange (V2.6)
Upload: all aliases sent with artifact (without is_preferred column)
Download: aliases received with source='aws', user sets preferred locally
Track upload verification: AWS returns existing area aliases, user picks standard name or keeps own
Dedup on import: matching source_unique_id adds PrimaryName as alias, not new record
4.4 Same Interaction All Artifacts
Click any artifact on map (trail, track, waypoint, route): detail panel shows all aliases with star/source/delete. Same pattern, same interaction, no exceptions.
Convoy map: display aliases, no actions
Planning map: display + add alias + set preferred + delete user alias
Waypoint creation proximity: display nearby aliases + add alias to existing
Work with Artifacts EDIT: full alias management
5. Spatial/Extension Sync Rules
Spatial tables are pure OGC standard. Extension tables are our app logic. Kotlin triggers maintain the relationship.
5.1 On Spatial Insert
Kotlin trigger: create matching properties row in extension table
Kotlin trigger: create first alias in artifact_aliases
Kotlin trigger: create data_log entry
Kotlin trigger: create tile_queue entry (priority by type)
5.2 On Spatial Delete
Kotlin trigger: delete matching properties row
Kotlin trigger: delete all aliases for this artifact
Kotlin trigger: delete survey if track
Kotlin trigger: remove from upload_queue if queued
Kotlin trigger: create data_log entry with before_state
5.3 On Extension Update
Kotlin trigger: update spatial.updated_at timestamp
Kotlin trigger: create data_log entry with before/after state
5.4 Never Allowed
No FKs on spatial tables (keeps them OGC standard)
No SQL triggers on spatial tables (all logic in Kotlin)
No direct extension table writes without matching spatial record
No orphaned extension records (Kotlin ensures sync)
6. Queue Lifecycle
6.1 Tile Queue
Owner: QueueManager + TileRequestTrigger
Created by: TileRequestTrigger on spatial insert/update
Priority: HIGH (tracks, routes), LOW (trails), MED (source refresh)
Processed by: existing tile download engine
On completion: QueueManager moves to transfer_history
6.2 Upload Queue
Owner: QueueManager
Created by: Share prompt YES on track/waypoint/route creation
V2.5: collects items (status='queued'). No processing.
V2.6: processes items. Pushes spatial + properties + aliases to AWS.
V2.6: AWS returns alias verification for tracks. User picks standard name.
On completion: QueueManager moves to transfer_history
6.3 Download Queue
Owner: QueueManager
V2.5: stubs only. No UI processing.
V2.6: user browses AWS by area. Selects items. Queue entry created.
V2.6: processes items. Pulls spatial + properties + aliases from AWS.
On download: TileRequestTrigger fires HIGH priority for new geometry
On completion: QueueManager moves to transfer_history
7. Version Implementation Gates

END OF LIFECYCLE OWNERSHIP DOCUMENT
GroupTrack V2.5 | May 18, 2026 | All sessions incorporated
Entity | Owns | Creates | Integrity
SpatialDbManager | Database creation, schema migration, open/close | grouptrack_spatial.spatialite + grouptrack_data.sqlite | Create extension row on spatial insert. Cascade delete extensions on spatial delete.

RouteManager | Route creation (draw/snap/convert). Trailhead validation. | routes + route_properties + artifact_aliases + data_log + tile_queue(HIGH) | trailhead_id nullable on create, required before ride release (V2.6). Block delete if ride assigned.
AliasManager | All alias operations across all artifact types. | artifact_aliases entries | Exactly one is_preferred per artifact. Min 1 alias always. Agency/AWS aliases undeletable.
QueueManager | All three queue tables. Status transitions. History moves. | tile_queue + upload_queue + download_queue + transfer_history | Queue entry on trigger (share, spatial insert). Move to history on completion.

=== GroupTrack_V25_ManualAddendum.docx ===
GroupTrack User Manual
Version 2.5 Addendum
Off-Road Convoy Tracking for Android
May 2026 | grouptrack.org
This addendum documents new and updated features in GroupTrack V2.5. It supplements the V2.4 User Manual. Chapter numbers reference the V2.4 manual structure. Updated chapters replace their V2.4 counterparts entirely.
Chapter 6. Work With Artifacts (replaces Display Panel)
V2.5 replaces the simple Display Panel with the Work with Artifacts panel, a comprehensive artifact management interface. The panel provides toggle controls for all four artifact types plus access to editing and import functions.
6.1 Opening Work With Artifacts
On the Planning Map, tap the WORK WITH ARTIFACTS button in the display area. The panel expands to show all artifact types with their counts and toggle controls.
On the Convoy Map, the same panel is available but in display-only mode. Editing and import functions are not available during live convoy operations.
6.2 Artifact Type Grid
The panel shows four artifact types in a grid layout. Each row displays the artifact type name, count, and a display toggle switch.
Trails
Toggle ON to display trail overlays from the spatial database. Trails are loaded dynamically based on your current map viewport. As you pan and zoom, trails update automatically. Only trails visible in your current view are loaded, ensuring smooth performance even with large trail datasets.
Trails appear as cyan (#00FFFF) solid lines with weight 4 on the map. Trail color varies by classification: blue for OHV/road-concurrent, orange for hiking/biking, yellow for hiking-only, purple for biking-only, and cyan for general/paved trails.
Trails load at zoom level 8 and above. At wider zoom levels, trails are not displayed to maintain map readability. Zoom in to see trail overlays.
Tracks
Toggle ON to display your recorded GPS tracks from the spatial database. Like trails, tracks are loaded dynamically based on your viewport. All tracks from your my_tracks/ library are automatically synced to the spatial database on app launch.
Tracks appear as neon green (#39FF14) dashed lines with weight 3 on the map. The dashed pattern distinguishes tracks from trails at a glance. Tracks persist on the map as you pan and zoom.
Waypoints (V2.5 In Progress)
Toggle for user-created waypoints. 10 standard waypoint types: trailhead, fuel, gate, hazard, scenic viewpoint, water source, camp, parking, rally point, and other. Each type has a distinct color and icon on the map.
Routes (V2.5 In Progress)
Toggle for planned routes including drawn routes, snap-to-trail routes, and imported route files.
6.3 Import Buttons
Two import buttons appear at the bottom of the Work with Artifacts panel on the Planning Map:
IMPORT TRAILS
Opens the trail source management screen where you can download trail databases from public land management agencies for your region. Trail data is stored in the spatial database for fast viewport-based display.
IMPORT ARTIFACTS
Opens a file picker to import GPX files from your Downloads folder. The import process automatically detects tracks, routes, and waypoints within the GPX file and inserts them into the appropriate spatial database tables. Tracks are also saved as GPX files in your my_tracks/ directory.
6.4 Trails and Tracks Together
Both Trails and Tracks can be displayed simultaneously. Trails render as solid cyan lines and tracks as dashed neon green lines, making them visually distinct even when overlapping. Toggle each independently using the display switches.
Trail and track data is queried from an on-device spatial database using bounding box intersection. Only artifacts within your current map viewport are loaded. This architecture supports thousands of trails and hundreds of tracks without performance degradation.

Chapter 9. Track Display (Updated for V2.5)
V2.5 introduces spatial database-backed track display with viewport-aware lazy loading. Tracks are automatically synced from your GPX files into the spatial database and displayed based on your current map viewport.
9.1 Automatic Track Sync
When you open the Planning Map, GroupTrack automatically scans your my_tracks/ directory and syncs any new GPX files into the spatial database. This one-time sync extracts track geometry and computes bounding boxes for fast viewport queries. Files already in the database are skipped.
The sync process runs in the background and does not block map interaction. New tracks appear on the map within seconds of the sync completing.
9.2 Viewport-Based Display
Unlike V2.4 which loaded all tracks sequentially from disk, V2.5 queries the spatial database for tracks whose bounding boxes intersect your current map viewport. This means only visible tracks are loaded and rendered, providing instant response even with large track libraries.
As you pan and zoom the map, the track query updates automatically with a 400-millisecond debounce to prevent excessive queries during rapid scrolling.
9.3 Track Appearance
Tracks display as dashed neon green lines (#39FF14) with a dash pattern of 10 pixels on, 5 pixels off, and a line weight of 3. This dashed pattern clearly distinguishes tracks from trails (solid lines) on the map.
Tapping a track line shows a popup with the track name. Track names are derived from the GPX filename.
9.4 Track Colors
All tracks displayed via the spatial database toggle appear in the standard neon green (#39FF14) dashed pattern. Individual track loading with color rotation is available through the TRACKS button on the Planning Map header (unchanged from V2.4).

Chapter 9A. Trail Display (New in V2.5)
V2.5 introduces spatial database-backed trail display. Trail data from public land management agencies is stored in an on-device GeoPackage/SQLite database and displayed dynamically based on your map viewport.
9A.1 Trail Data Coverage
The current release includes trail data for southern Utah and northern Arizona, covering the St. George to Grand Canyon corridor. This includes OHV trails, multi-use trails, hiking paths, and paved shared-use paths from USFS, BLM, and state land management agencies.
Additional state and regional trail datasets will be available for download in future updates through the Trail Source Management screen.
9A.2 Trail Appearance
Trails display as solid cyan lines (#00FFFF) with a line weight of 4. Trail color varies by CartoCode classification:
Blue (#00AAFF): OHV and road-concurrent trails (CartoCode 4) with weight 5 for emphasis.
Orange (#FF8800): Hiking and biking trails (CartoCode 2).
Yellow (#FFCC00): Hiking-only trails (CartoCode 1).
Purple (#AA44FF): Biking-only trails (CartoCode 5).
Cyan (#00FFFF): Default for unclassified or paved shared-use trails.
9A.3 Viewport-Based Loading
Trails load dynamically as you pan and zoom the map. The spatial database uses bounding box indexing to rapidly identify trails visible in your current viewport. Trails appear at zoom level 8 and above.
At wide zoom levels (below 8), trails are not displayed to maintain map readability and prevent performance issues from loading thousands of trail segments simultaneously.
9A.4 Trail Properties
Each trail in the database includes properties from the originating land management agency: primary name, surface type (paved, unpaved, gravel), designated uses (motor, hike, horse, bike), motorized access status, trail class, steward organization, and county. These properties are available in the trail detail panel when tapping a trail on the map (coming in a future update).

Chapter 10. Download Queue (Updated for V2.5)
V2.5 enhances the download queue with management controls including hold, resume, cancel individual entries, and cancel all operations.
10.1 Queue Management Controls
The WORK WITH QUEUES button on both the Convoy Map and Planning Map opens the queue management panel. The panel shows active, queued, and completed download entries.
Hold Queue
Pause all queue processing. Active downloads complete their current tile but no new tiles are started and no queued items begin processing. Use this when you need bandwidth for other activities.
Resume Queue
Resume queue processing after a hold. Paused downloads continue from where they stopped and queued items begin processing.
Cancel Entry
Cancel an individual download entry. The entry is removed from the queue and any in-progress tiles for that entry stop downloading. Downloaded tiles for the partially completed entry are preserved on disk.
Cancel All
Stop all active downloads and clear the entire queue. All in-progress downloads stop immediately. Previously downloaded tiles are preserved.
Queue management controls are fully functional in the backend. The queue panel UI is being wired to live data in the next update.

Appendix C. V2.5 Feature Status
This appendix replaces V2.4 Appendix C with the current status of V2.5 features.
C.1 Completed Features
C.2 In Progress
C.3 Planned for V2.5 (Not Yet Started)
C.4 Deferred to V2.6 / V3.0

5. Key Architecture Decisions (Settled)
5.1 Databases
grouptrack_trails.db: Public agency trail data. SQLite. Read-only. Downloaded on-demand. FREE.
grouptrack_user.spatialite: Personal data. SpatiaLite. Read-write. Waypoints, routes, tracks, tile sources, journal.

5.2 Entity Models
Waypoint identity: Coordinates (lon/lat). Names are aliases in waypoint_aliases table. Rename creates alias. Delete removes alias. Waypoint deleted when no aliases remain.
Track identity: GPX/KML file. Names in track_aliases. Same alias/delete model as waypoints. Primary alias rename cascades to route name.
Route: Never independently shared. Sharing controlled by configurable app_setting.
Trail: Never individually deleted. Source/region removal only. Display toggle, not deletion.
Area delete: Removes tiles only (biggest storage). Spatial data stays.

5.3 Ownership and Delete
Creator delete cascades to collective (V3.0). Non-creator delete removes local alias only. Local deletes do not impact shared data unless removing something I created.

5.4 Sync Model
Offline-first. All local changes queue outbound in strict chronological order. Local DB only updated during explicit user-initiated data pulls. One process syncs all downloaded areas.

5.5 Data Protection
Three layers: automatic backup (launch + pre-destructive, last 5), change journal (every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with before/after JSON + geometry WKT, 30-day retention), rollback (single-op undo, transaction, point-in-time).

5.6 Map Source Model
map_sources.json defines all sources with layers, validation rules, cache dirs. Code is generic - reads JSON, executes rules. No source-specific logic. User can add custom sources after validation passes.

5.7 GroupTrack as Awareness Conduit
Not a data provider. Catalog of public URLs at grouptrack.org. Nightly cron checks for source updates (HEAD requests). Users download from agencies directly. Each device unique to rider needs.

6. Schema Reference
grouptrack_user_schema_v2.sql is the hardened schema with 20 tables/views and 24 lifecycle trigger placeholders. Every trigger has exact business rules documented in SQL comments with source quotes. Schema committed to docs/.

Key tables: tile_sources, map_slots, source_layers, waypoints, waypoint_aliases, waypoint_types, routes, tracks, track_aliases, ride_areas, source_ingestions, transfer_queue, change_journal, backup_log, data_log, dedup_log, app_settings.

Key rules in triggers: waypoint proximity check (25m), no waypoint moves, rename creates alias, delete through aliases with orphan cleanup, track name cascade to route, area delete = tiles only, share validation against ride.private, route sharing controlled by app_settings, outbound sync queuing.

7. Standing Rules (20)
1. Never auto-delete user data. 2. Never embed API keys. 3. Share is opt-in. 4. Offline-first. 5. Canvas independence. 6. Cumulative collection. 7. Routes never independently public. 8. Private rides block sharing. 9. Published content recoverable. 10. Trails/routes never individually removed. 11. First source wins dedup. 12. Ops/Dialogs pattern. 13. Every change journaled. 14. Backup before destructive ops. 15. Journal stores before+after+WKT. 16. Schema before code. 17. Triggers before features. 18. Patch scripts uniquely versioned. 19. Never commit flags=true. 20. Preserve geometry precision.
8. Hardware Restrictions
1. T1000-E firmware: LOCK to 2.6.11 max. Newer destabilizes BLE + radio config.
2. Radio stays in cart during rides. Keep within 50ft BLE range. Exceeding causes supervision timeout pauses.
9. Reference Documents (in docs/)

GroupTrack V2.5 Session Handoff
May 11, 2026 -- Download Queue + Queue Panel + Performance

1. Commits This Session (5)
2. Download Queue Architecture
2.1 Components
2.2 Key Design Decisions
WorkManager for background execution -- downloads survive app backgrounding, screen rotation, device sleep.
Max 2 concurrent downloads. Queue processes in priority order.
Progress updates: StateFlow only, no disk I/O. Status changes (complete/failed/cancelled) save to JSON.
Notification update interval: every 250 tiles (was 50). Reduces system overhead.
Queue panel at BottomStart, 280dp wide, clear of download panel at BottomEnd.
Esri tiles confirmed -- zero Google URLs in codebase. Download URLs verified on device.
3. Download Queue Priority -- Design Rule

Source refresh trigger: when user changes a tile source for a map slot, app detects existing downloaded regions. Prompts: 'Refresh to new source?' If yes, queues priority-7 refresh entries. New downloads (priority 3) always service before refreshes (priority 7). Refresh may take days. This is user-triggered, not automatic. Respects Standing Rule 1.

GroupTrack V2.4 / V2.5
Session Handoff Document

1. Current Build State
The V2.4 release build compiles successfully but has one critical blocker: the Tracks display toggle crashes the app when toggled ON because convoyLoadTrack() reads 68 GPX/KML files synchronously on the main thread, causing an ANR kill.

Last committed build: 0c9d67953 (before tracks load-all)
This build is stable and deployable. All features work except the tracks display toggle (which was not wired to load tracks at that point).

Latest build (uncommitted): tracks load-all + grey-out fix
After the crash was discovered, the Tracks toggle was greyed out as V2.5. A build is running with this fix. If successful, this is the release candidate.

1.1 What Works (Confirmed by Testing)
1.2 What Does NOT Work (Blockers)
1.3 UI Polish Issues (Non-blocking)
2. Tracks Display Toggle - Detailed Fix Plan
2.1 Root Cause
The app has TWO separate track systems in JavaScript:
- trackLines[] - live GPS recording track, drawn by drawTrack(), toggled by toggleTracks()
- importedTracks{} - saved track files loaded by loadTrackFile(), toggled by toggleTrackFiles() (Planning Map) or showTracks()/hideTracks() (Convoy Map, after our JS fix)

The crash occurs because convoyLoadTrack() in ConvoyScreen.kt reads files synchronously:
fun convoyLoadTrack(context, fileName, color, webView) {
    val text = file.readText()  // BLOCKS MAIN THREAD
    val coords = convoyParseGpx(text)  // BLOCKS MAIN THREAD
    webView?.evaluateJavascript("loadTrackFile(...)", null)
}

With 68 files, this blocks the main thread for 60+ seconds, triggering Android's ANR watchdog which kills the app.
2.2 Fix: Async Track Loading
The fix is to wrap all file I/O in a coroutine on Dispatchers.IO, then post the JavaScript call back to Main:

ConvoyScreen.kt tracks toggle callback:
onTracksToggle = {
    tracksVisible = !tracksVisible
    if (tracksVisible) {
        if (tracksLoaded) {
            webViewRef.value?.evaluateJavascript("showTracks()", null)
        } else {
            tracksLoaded = true
            kotlinx.coroutines.MainScope().launch {
                val dir = java.io.File(Environment.getExternalStoragePublicDirectory(
                    Environment.DIRECTORY_DOCUMENTS), "my_tracks")
                val files = dir.listFiles()?.map { it.name }?.sorted() ?: emptyList()
                files.forEachIndexed { idx, name ->
                    val color = colors[idx % colors.size]
                    withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
                        val text = File(dir, name).readText()
                        val coords = if (name.endsWith(".gpx")) convoyParseGpx(text)
                            else convoyParseKml(text)
                        val json = coords.joinToString(",", "[", "]") { ... }
                        withContext(Dispatchers.Main) {
                            webViewRef.value?.evaluateJavascript(
                                "loadTrackFile('$name', '$json', '$color')", null)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    } else {
        webViewRef.value?.evaluateJavascript("hideTracks()", null)
    }
}

The same pattern applies to ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt using loadTrackOnMap() which already uses MainScope().launch with Dispatchers.IO (see line 693). The Planning Map version should work correctly once wired because loadTrackOnMap is already async.

Key difference: loadTrackOnMap() in MapViewerScreen is already async (uses MainScope().launch + Dispatchers.IO). convoyLoadTrack() in ConvoyScreen is synchronous. Either make convoyLoadTrack async, or use loadTrackOnMap's pattern.

7. Standing Development Rules
8. Key Architecture Decisions
- Two separate WebViews: convoy_map.html (convoy map) and grouptrack_map.html (Planning Map) with separate JavaScript state
- Tracks are NOT shared between WebViews - loading on Planning Map does not affect convoy map
- Display panel is a shared Compose component (ConvoyDisplayPanel.kt) used on both maps with different callbacks
- ConvoyMapBar is a shared component with nav button, source buttons, and NET/LOCAL toggle
- Download queue uses WorkManager for background processing with notification support
- Map tile sources are data-driven via MapSourceManager reading map_sources.json
- V2.4 is the iOS port source - WebView HTML/JS assets port directly to PWA
- iPad version: fork Meshtastic web client, deploy as PWA through Web Bluetooth browser (Bluefy)
- V3.0 subscription ($3/month) via Google Play + Apple IAP when PWA wraps in Capacitor
- Remove Area reuses download queue (QueueType.REMOVE) with red shadow color
- Three shadow colors on map: blue (downloaded), pink (downloading), red (removing)

GroupTrack � Task Status Handoff
May 13, 2026
V2.4 Deployed | V2.5 Implementation In Progress | V3.0 Debug on Android 2
1. V2.4 Deployment � Completed Items

2. V2.5 Implementation � Open Items
All V2.5 work follows this process for each task: (1) Plan � discuss scope, define deliverables, agree on boundaries. (2) Research � search field cross-ref, function universe, where-used to identify every impacted file and function. (3) Agree � confirm impact analysis is complete, no hidden references. (4) Build � one patch, one test, one commit.

2.1 Task 1: Source Picker (NEXT)
Status: NOT STARTED � detailed planning required before beginning
Objective: Expose all 16 map sources from map_sources.json to user selection. Users pick which source fills each of the 3 map slots.
The 16 sources are built-in defaults shipping with the app. No custom source entry, no API key input, no validation � all pre-verified in JSON. Users select from the catalog to replace slot assignments.

Scope:
� UI: Long-press map bar heading opens source picker. Shows 16 sources grouped by type (SAT, HYB, TOPO, STREET, TERRAIN, OUTDOOR). Tap to assign to slot.
� Display: Selected source URL drives setTileUrl for online display. Cache directory from JSON drives offline tile serving.
� Download: Selected source layers drive tile downloads. Multi-layer sources (SAT = 3 layers) download all layers. Single-layer sources download 1.
� Persistence: Slot assignments saved. Survive app restart.
� Map Viewer only: Convoy map stays on defaults until cutover.

2.2 Task 2: Download Queue
Status: NOT STARTED � builds on source picker
Objective: Replace direct download with queued, managed downloads. 2 concurrent. Resumable. Cancellable. Self-healing background refresh.
Testers launch multiple download requests because downloads are slow. Requests pile up causing ANRs. Queue accepts all requests, processes 2 at a time, shows progress, supports cancel and resume.

Components: DownloadQueueManager (singleton), QueueEntry (data class), Queue UI Panel (progress bars, cancel, history), resume logic (persist queue, scan on restart), self-healing background refresh (low-priority re-download of existing areas).
Ships as V2.4 patch release with source picker. Testers get faster, reliable downloads.

2.3 Task 3: Spatial Database � Trails
Status: NOT STARTED � Python POC proven (46,953 Utah trails)
Objective: Load SpatiaLite database with Utah state trails and user tracks. Replace GeoJSON asset loading with spatial viewport queries.

Components:
� Kotlin ingestion engine (ConvoyTrailOps.kt) porting Python POC
� grouptrack_trails.db: public agency trail data, read-only after ingestion
� Trail source catalog with user-selectable filters (OHV default)
� Download from agency URLs (UGRC), ingest on-device
� Viewport queries lazy-load trails to map
� Replace utah_trails_stgeorge.geojson asset with database queries
� Dedup on ingestion with review screen

2.4 Task 4: Spatial Database � Tracks
Status: NOT STARTED
Objective: Index user tracks (GPX/KML files) in grouptrack_user.spatialite. Track alias model. Display from spatial data.

Components:
� Track metadata + bbox in user database (spatial index, not file copy)
� Track alias model matching waypoints (identity = file, names in track_aliases)
� Primary alias rename cascades to route name
� File sync on launch reconciles DB with filesystem
� Display switches from direct file parse to spatial query

2.5 Task 5: Waypoints
Status: NOT STARTED
Objective: Long-press waypoint creation on map. Type picker. Alias model. Proximity check.

Components:
� Reclaim long-press for waypoint creation (move source picker to RIDERS button or separate UI)
� 10 waypoint types with icons (trailhead, fuel, gate, hazard, scenic, water, camp, parking, rally, other)
� Alias model: identity = coordinates, names in waypoint_aliases
� Proximity check on creation (25m)
� No moves (delete and recreate). No consolidation (delete the extra).
� Map legend from waypoint_types table
� Share prompt

2.6 Task 6: Routes
Status: NOT STARTED
Objective: Route creation, editing, and assignment. Never independently shared.

� Create by: draw on map, snap-to-trail, convert from track, import GPX/KML
� Route sharing controlled by configurable app_setting
� Never independently shared � only through ride enrollment (V3.0)
� source_track_id links converted tracks to routes

2.7 Task 7: Area Management
Status: NOT STARTED
Objective: Viewport-based download areas. Block-based queued downloads. Storage overlays.

� Viewport zoom defines download areas
� Smart first pull guided by trail coverage
� Area overlays: blue fill (tiles) + black diagonal stripes (spatial data)
� Area delete removes tiles only. Spatial data stays.

4.1 MapSourceManager.kt (commit e8c0c6cd8)
Single source of truth for all tile URLs. Reads map_sources.json from assets. 16 built-in sources, 3 configurable slots. Serves display URLs, download layers, offline cache directories. Replaced 17 hardcoded references across 6 files. Fixed Google URL bug in download handler.

4.2 map_sources.json
16 tile sources: Google (4), Esri (5), USGS (2), OpenTopoMap, OpenStreetMap, CalTopo, Thunderforest, CartoDB. Default slots: SAT (Esri Imagery+Overlays), TOPO (Esri World Topo), TOPO+ (Esri USA Topo). Custom source template included for future use.

4.3 Schema v2 (grouptrack_user_schema_v2.sql)
20 tables/views, 24 lifecycle trigger placeholders with exact business rules in SQL comments. Key tables: tile_sources, map_slots, source_layers, waypoints, waypoint_aliases, waypoint_types, routes, tracks, track_aliases, ride_areas, source_ingestions, transfer_queue, change_journal, backup_log, app_settings. Schema hardened. Ready for implementation.

4.4 Trail Ingestion POC (build_trails_db_v1.py)
Python script proven with full Utah state data: 49,096 features yielded 46,953 trails. 18,230 OHV/motorized, 26,224 multi-use, 2,499 hiking. 107MB database. St George viewport: 535 trails. Ready for Kotlin port.

5. Standing Rules (21)
1. Never auto-delete user data. 2. Never embed API keys. 3. Share is opt-in. 4. Offline-first. 5. Canvas independence. 6. Cumulative collection. 7. Routes never independently public. 8. Private rides block sharing. 9. Published content recoverable. 10. Trails/routes never individually removed. 11. First source wins dedup. 12. Ops/Dialogs pattern. 13. Every change journaled. 14. Backup before destructive ops. 15. Journal stores before+after+WKT. 16. Schema before code. 17. Triggers before features. 18. Patch scripts uniquely versioned. 19. Never commit flags=true. 20. Preserve geometry precision. 21. Complete impact analysis before ANY code change � grep every field, URL, function name across entire codebase. Document every consumer. No exceptions.
6. Development Process
For every task, before any code is written:
1. PLAN � Detailed discussion. Define scope and deliverables. Agree on what is in and what is out.
2. RESEARCH � Search field cross-ref, function universe, where-used to identify every file and function impacted. Trace every field value through its consumers.
3. AGREE � Confirm impact analysis is complete. No hidden references. No unknown consumers.
4. BUILD � One patch, one test, one commit. Build and test after each change. No stacking patches.

All 16 map sources are built-in defaults selected at build time. Custom sources with user API keys come later. Source picker selects from the existing JSON catalog only.

=== GroupTrack_V25_SessionHandoff_May16.docx ===
GroupTrack � ANR Investigation Handoff
May 16, 2026
V2.4 Deployed | ANR Investigation on P10_T | V3.0 Debug Pending on Android 2
1. Builds Completed Today
2. Code Changes Applied
2.1 WorkManager ANR Fix (fix_workmanager_anr_v1.py)
File: MeshUtilApplication.kt
Changed ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE to KEEP � prevents MeshLogCleanupWorker from re-triggering on every cold start
Added 30-second initial delay to PeriodicWorkRequest � first-ever run does not compete with cold start initialization
Added import for java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit
2.2 WorkManager Prune Fix (fix_workmanager_prune_v2.py)
File: MeshUtilApplication.kt
Added WorkManager.getInstance(this).pruneWork() before scheduleMeshLogCleanup() � clears stale finished/cancelled/failed work entries on every cold start
Addresses accumulated WorkManager jobs from previous installs/sideloads that survive uninstall
2.3 Commit Status
Changes committed to feature/convoy-event-ride branch. Version code bumped to 29320500 for Play Store upload. V3_FEATURES_ENABLED restored to false.
3. ANR Investigation � P10_T Device
3.1 Device Profile
3.2 Comparison: Android 2 vs P10_T (Same Play Store Build)
3.3 ANR Types Identified
ANR Type 1: WorkManager onStartJob (FIXED)
SystemJobService.onStartJob() not responding within timeout. Caused by MeshLogCleanupWorker re-triggering on every cold start via ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE. Four duplicate ANRs, four "Exempted app considered buggy" warnings. Fixed by KEEP policy + pruneWork + initial delay.
ANR Type 2: Input Dispatching Timeout (OPEN)
MainActivity not responding to MotionEvent within 10 seconds. Main thread blocked for 20-43 seconds after "Binding to mesh service" with zero log output. Occurs during Meshtastic Getting Started screen before any convoy/planning map code runs.
ANR Type 3: Zombie Process (IDENTIFIED)
Old GroupTrack process "refused to die" preventing new launch. System waits 10 seconds, cancels new process, returns to desktop. MeshService foreground service with wake lock and BLE connections keeps old process alive. Killing PID manually allows relaunch. Secondary symptom, not root cause.
4. Root Cause Analysis � PRIMARY FINDING
4.1 osmdroid Tile Cache Scanning
Strongest hypothesis: osmdroid cache management is scanning/trimming 60 GB of tile data during Application.onCreate() on the main thread.
Evidence:
Factory reset (zero tiles) = fast launch. Over time as tester downloads tiles = progressively slower launch. Pattern confirmed across multiple resets.
Android 2 (zero tiles) launches same Play Store build in 1 second. P10_T (~60 GB tiles) takes 20-31 seconds.
osmdroid config in MeshUtilApplication.onCreate() sets tileFileSystemCacheMaxBytes = 1 GB but actual tile data is ~60 GB. osmdroid may attempt to trim from 60 GB to 1 GB on startup.
Main thread goes completely silent for 20-43 seconds during startup � consistent with filesystem scanning that produces no log output.
Clearing app data, resetting app preferences, uninstall/reinstall/reboot do NOT fix it � because tile files are on external storage and survive all of these operations.
4.2 Key Insight: osmdroid Does Not Cache Local Tiles
GroupTrack serves tiles via a custom convoy://tiles/ URL scheme intercepted in shouldInterceptRequest. These tiles are managed by GroupTrack, not by osmdroid. osmdroid should not be scanning or managing this tile directory at all. The osmdroid cache configuration in onCreate() may be inadvertently pointing to or scanning the GroupTrack tile directory.
4.3 Verification In Progress
Attempting to rename tiles directory on P10_T to prove the hypothesis. The mv command is running but taking time due to Android FUSE layer processing hundreds of thousands of directory entries. If the app launches fast with tiles renamed, the cause is confirmed.
5. Proposed Fix
Option 1 (Preferred): Disable osmdroid Cache Trimming
Since GroupTrack manages its own tiles via convoy://tiles/ and does not use osmdroid for tile caching, disable osmdroid's built-in cache management entirely. Either remove the tileFileSystemCacheMaxBytes/tileFileSystemCacheTrimBytes configuration, or set them to very high values, or point osmdroid's cache to a separate empty directory that GroupTrack does not use.
Option 2: Defer Cache Init to Background Thread
Move osmdroid Configuration.getInstance() calls off the main thread in MeshUtilApplication.onCreate(). Wrap in a coroutine on Dispatchers.IO. This reduces ANR risk but does not eliminate the unnecessary 60 GB scan.
Option 3: Instrumented Debug Build
If the tile rename test is inconclusive, build a debug APK with timing instrumentation at every startup step: Application.onCreate(), each content provider, BootCompleteReceiver, MeshService.onCreate(), permission callbacks, and osmdroid initialization. Install on P10_T and identify the exact blocking call with millisecond precision.

=== GroupTrack_V25_SpatialArchitecture_v1.docx ===
GroupTrack V2.5
Spatial Architecture Planning
Decisions captured May 9, 2026 | Do not re-litigate
1. Architecture overview
GroupTrack separates map canvas (tile imagery) from spatial data (trails, waypoints, routes, tracks). The canvas is user-configurable � riders pick their own tile sources and manage their own API keys. GroupTrack never embeds, distributes, or licenses tile source keys. The spatial data layer is GroupTrack's product.

1.1 Two databases
grouptrack_trails.spatialite � shipped asset, free, public. Official agency trail data (UGRC, BLM, USFS). Read-only on device. Lazy loads to map viewport via spatial index. Always available, no download step, no area boundaries. Updated when GroupTrack ships a new release. This is what gets riders in the door.
grouptrack_user.spatialite � rider's data, read-write. Waypoints, routes, tracks collected through rider activity. Downloaded via ride enrollment in V3.0. Shared through the ride engine when subscription activates. Survives app updates and uninstalls (stored in /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/data/).

1.2 Canvas independence
GroupTrack ships 12 default tile sources: 3 satellite, 3 topo, 3 road, 3 trail. All free, no API key required (except Thunderforest Outdoors which has a free key). Users add their own sources � CalTopo, Gaia, onX subscribers enter their own URL template and API key. If a tile source goes offline or changes pricing, the user deletes or updates the entry. GroupTrack is completely out of the tile sourcing business.
The Esri migration question (V25 Backlog Seq 19) drops in priority permanently. Canvas selection is a user preference, not a GroupTrack dependency.

1.3 Design principles
Offline-first: all spatial data downloads to the device before the rider leaves connectivity. No lazy loading in the field except trails (which are always local).
Cumulative collection: rider's local database grows over time. Primary area download plus ride enrollments add data. Nothing removed without explicit user action.
No auto-delete: NEVER programmatically delete user files. All deletes require explicit user action with confirmation.
Share is opt-in: the 'share' flag on tracks, waypoints, and routes is always a deliberate user action, never automatic.

2. Map overlay model
2.1 Visual patterns
Blue fill: tiles downloaded for this area. Existing behavior, unchanged from V2.4.
Black diagonal stripes: waypoints, routes, and tracks present for this area. New in V2.5.
Blue + black stripes: complete offline coverage � both tiles and spatial data.
Stripes only (no blue): spatial data present but no offline tiles � rider has trail-related data but map imagery loads from network only.
One area outline serves both tile and spatial boundaries. The same drawn polygon defines both coverages.

2.2 Show controls
Both Planning Map and convoy map display the coverage overlays. Two toggle buttons: 'Tiles' and 'Spatial' (labeled as waypoints, routes, tracks). Rider can show one or both. Convoy map shows only � no create, no delete. Planning Map is the management hub.

2.3 Area management � Planning Map only
Five actions, all on Planning Map (renamed from Map Viewer in V2.5): Draw area (polygon on map), Download (tiles and/or spatial for drawn area), Refresh (re-download updated data for existing area), Remove (delete tiles and/or spatial within drawn area), Queue (view transfer manager).
All download and area management functionality is removed from convoy map in V2.5. Convoy map is purely operational � it shows coverage overlays, renders trails, displays riders, and records tracks. No downloads, no area editing, no queue access. Clean HUD for ride time.
