⭐ ROUTE-STATE PERSISTENCE &amp; TEARDOWN (this morning's issue) OPEN
Root cause located 07-06 via fresh xref (recommit docs; navigation_xref regenerated 07-06 11:32). Fix design not yet locked — one source-check remains.
Problem (observed)
The route nav box disappears; states don't change as they should. Route-planning state is not reliably persisted across navigation, nor reliably torn down on exit. Two repro triggers (with a route open): (a) open/touch another item; (b) close the artifacts panel. Two failure modes: (1) route disappears from the map entirely; (2) route stays drawn but goes dead/inert (geometry visible, controls gone/unresponsive).
Root cause (located from xref)
Route mode is held in var routeMode by remember { mutableStateOf(false) } — ephemeral Compose state — at TWO independent copies: ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:129 and ConvoyScreen.kt:197. Both drive ONE shared window.__routeMode in convoy_map.html. Teardown = ~8 scattered hardcoded calls per screen of setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine(); (ConvoyMapViewerScreen 955/1044/1075/1112, arm-on 996/1020, resume 1154; ConvoyScreen 1608/1684/1716/1743, arm-on 1648/1671, resume 1775). No single teardown funnel.
This one fact explains both failure modes: touching another item / closing the panel recomposes or orphans the remember boolean → Kotlin routeMode resets/desyncs but JS gets NO matching setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine(). Disappear = a path fired clearBuildLine / a redraw overlaid it. Stays-but-dead = Kotlin routeMode went false so controls detach, but JS still shows the line.
Intent — Fred's 3 requirements
  Persist route-planning state in the MAP JSON so nav away + back restores it (survives recomposition/nav, which remember does not).
  States unique per map — Planning (grouptrack_map.html) vs Convoy (convoy_map.html) must not collide on the shared JS flag; the two booleans need per-map identity.
  Every exit ends it — save, discard, navigate away, back, mode-switch, backgrounding, item-tap, panel-close — via ONE teardown funnel every exit routes through (replacing the ~8 scattered teardowns).
Key principle: persist unless/until closed by an exit method — persist across nav, never past an exit.
Touchpoints + remaining source-check before locking
Touchpoints: setRouteMode (JS, convoy_map.html) toggled from both screens; window.__routeMode gate if(window.__routeMode)return; at convoy_map.html:495 (BUG A popup suppression — must stay mode-scoped); RouteManager holds build logic (snap/addVertex/undoVertex/clearRoute/routeVertices, buildWktAndBbox, insertRoute); JS build fns drawBuildLine/clearBuildLine/updateRoutes/showRoutes; onTrackTap at ConvoyMapViewerScreen:515, ConvoyScreen:645 &amp; 895.
Before locking: the xref indexes definitions + bridge calls, not full handler bodies. Read the actual .kt for the artifact-panel-close (onDismiss/onClose) handler + the onTrackTap bodies and CONFIRM they lack a setRouteMode(false) teardown call (the diagnosis predicts they do). Then design = persist route state to the map JSON (per-map keyed) + single teardown funnel every exit routes through. Lock only after the two-handler read confirms.
LEAD TRACK / TICK / MY-CART REWRITE (ITEM C — needs radio, LAST) SETTLED, NOT STARTED
Spec: GroupTrack_LeadCart_TrackRevision_DemolitionRebuild_2026-06-18.md (authority: LeadTrackReplacement_Spec.docx May 31). Problem: lead broadcasts position over radio; code reconstructs path + fills gaps with projection → phantom carts on rebroadcast (worst on switchbacks); three parallel track-drawing flows compete.
Demolition (part 1)
Find via fresh xref + dual-language grep + 2-cart field capture, then remove: the 3 parallel LIVE-track flows leadTrackSegments/gpsTrailSegments/routeTrailSegments + trackLeadOnly (~ConvoyScreen 345-350); live drawTrack(...); the lead-lock engine in ConvoyEngine (evaluateLeadLock, tick()→compute()→assignLeadTail(), lockedLeadNodeId, _leadLockedFlag — retire tick-oscillation: two tick entries/cycle ~170ms apart); all projection/proxy substitution (phantom source); per-node live segment-coloring. Do NOT touch: displayed/imported DB tracks (loadTracks/trackLayer), node markers, route lines, route-builder snap-2.
Rebuild (part 2) + rates + new reqs
(1) track ONLY the lead cart from broadcasts; (2) snap-2 100-yd radius onto known trail geometry; (3) every other cart = present-position marker only, NOT tracked (kills phantom at root); (4) each cart records own GPS and as it overtakes the lead's positions REPLACES the lead's path on its own map with own GPS. Net = one continuous trail improving in accuracy toward the rear.
Rates (supersede spec): lead broadcast ~4s (spec 5s); self-record 2s change-gated (spec 1s). Don't fake smoothness with projection. New reqs: remove "track all carts" toggle; lead cart picked from a list unless only 1 displayed (auto-lead); reassignable in cart HUD; lead segment (new pushTrackToMap, 0 refs = single draw/update entry) gets configurable color + weight. Open: overtake overwrite unconditional vs snap-gated (coarse lead data argues snap-gated) — confirm vs May-31 spec. Related: two concurrent ConvoyViewModel instances; cart-identity bug (startGroupTrack stores "!phone").
Recorder items (needs radio, ITEM C cluster) OPEN
  2s change-gated sampling (supersedes 1s) — tick 2s; write a GPX point ONLY if moved beyond a threshold (a few meters / snap-2 min — not any-delta, else stationary jitter writes noise). Why not 1s: no snap coverage like onX; onX ~3s. Pairs with Doppler max-speed. ConvoyGpsService interval. Helps only NEW tracks.
  Capture + store max speed during recording, write on save (Doppler each update, track max live). Recorded not derived → glitch gone.
  Android-GPS recording bug (Android-only fails; radio-create certified 06-30). ConvoyGpsService.kt (CRLF): startLocationUpdates (~251-277 prime suspect), onGpsUpdate (~288). Instrument first. + recorder truncation (no &lt;/trk&gt; on interrupt — record-stop must finalize the file).
Other V2.6 backlog (no-radio) OPEN
  ⚠ MAPS checkbox ignored when track already exists — fires only in the INSERT branch; move the maps call out of AddOutcome.INSERT -&gt; and gate on the checkbox for any non-error outcome.
  Draw/connect tracks into a route — (a) free-draw by tapping; (b) connect existing tracks at suggested connection points (detect endpoint proximity, suggest join, stitch). (b)-leaning; scope not locked. Reuses route machinery (RouteManager, ConvoyRouteToolbar, snap-2, bbox) + a new "suggest connection points."

V2.7 — iPad / CROSS-PLATFORM (post-V2.6 target)
Standing awareness — not an active task. iPad IS the post-V2.6 target (this overturns the old V3.0 "no iPad support" line). Reasoning arc reconciled 07-04. The evolution below is written in so it's never lost.
The reconciled strategy (07-04) STRATEGY
  Key collapse: Convoy is a fork of Meshtastic's messaging (Android = a fork of Meshtastic-Android, Kotlin). The native-vs-PWA-vs-WKWebView arc was all answering "how do we get BLE on iOS?" — a question that dissolves once convoy is seen as a fork of the mesh app. So iPad = a fork of Meshtastic-Apple (Swift/SwiftUI + BLE + protobuf; GPL v3; App-Store-approved; universal). Mac + Xcode = the prerequisite. Flag: Meshtastic-Apple ships native TAK/CoT — reconcile vs the roadmap's "TAK as pattern only."
  Config write is offloaded: the planning side CREATES a Meshtastic restore FILE (pure file creation, no BLE in GroupTrack's code); Meshtastic's own "restore config" applies it. Confirm the backup/restore format + Apple acceptance at build time.
  Presentation ~90% shared because it's already web (Leaflet in a WebView). SwiftUI rejected for presentation — it doesn't port to a browser + gives zero reuse of the Android web layer. iPad presentation = the existing web layer in a WKWebView behind a native Swift shell; PC = the same web (planning half) in a browser; Android = the same web unchanged. Swift's only job = the native shell (mesh source + WebView host + JS↔native bridge, the WKScriptMessageHandler analog of Android's JavascriptInterface).
  Real cost driver = the bridge/I/O surface. What renders inside the WebView ports cleanly; every point where the web reaches out to the device (file I/O, GPS, radio/mesh, camera, share, persistence, offline-tile reads, native dialogs) is a bridge call re-implemented per platform, many with no browser equivalent (why PC is planning-only). Next action: enumerate that surface from the Android code (every JavascriptInterface method + evaluateJavascript/postMessage crossing) — = the true iPad build cost AND which functions can/can't go to PC.
  Three surfaces split on connectivity: PC = planning-only web app (routes/waypoints/library + config-file generation; no mesh/radio; online); Android + iPad = off-grid native convoy execution (BLE/radio/live mesh — convoy cannot be web). The A/B decision touches only the mobile mesh source; PC proceeds independently.
  Two candidate iPad-execution patterns (open): (A) BRIDGE — convoy is its own native iOS app consuming mesh over a local loopback port from the separate Meshtastic app (less code; adds a runtime dependency + iOS-lifecycle fragility — the neighbor app must stay foregrounded, a real mark against A for an off-grid safety app); (B) FORK — import Meshtastic's BLE/mesh and extend, exactly as on Android (more work; no runtime dependency; Android-sameness). Not decided; off-grid reliability leans B.
  Target end-state: a messaging/logic SERVICE LAYER + logic-free presentation panels (panels call the service for everything). Serving all three platforms = the logic rewritten ONCE into one platform-independent implementation, not three copies. Current code isn't built this way (logic woven into the Android fork) → a one-time extraction = the same effort as the bridge-surface inventory seen from the other end.
  KMP is the natural target: logic is already Kotlin; KMP migration is incremental (share networking/data/domain first; expect/actual IS the "configured API resolves per platform" idea). KMP produces a shared logic module a Swift UI/shell consumes (it does NOT fork Meshtastic-Apple — that's Swift). Readiness gauge: (1) mechanical — KMP plugin preflight + Qodana; (2) architectural — a logic-entanglement inventory vs where_used/function_universe xref (the real effort predictor).
Sequencing (firm) + next-session deliverables STRATEGY
  Ship V2.6 on Windows (cleanup + map-download rewrite).
  Set up the Mac Air and build/run known-good V2.6 on it FIRST — prove the environment with a known-good artifact before piling on KMP.
  Then KMP plugin preflight + the entanglement inventory vs xref.
  Then incremental KMP extraction (share domain/logic first).
  Then iPad.
Rule: do NOT introduce KMP onto an unproven Mac — one unknown at a time (else a break is ambiguous between KMP and Mac setup). Building V2.6 on Mac is the first rung needed anyway (same env for preflight + eventual Xcode).
Deliverable 1 — Mac environment build-out: inventory required tools + install-and-confirm one at a time (Git + Terminal/zsh — macOS is real Unix, the Git-Bash/CRLF-heredoc pain may relax; Android Studio + SDK + Gradle + JDK/JavaVM; Python; keystore access — grouptrack-release-key.jks is in iCloud; clone + build V2.6; THEN the KMP plugin; MySQL — purpose TBD; Xcode + Apple Developer enrollment — later rung, iPad only). Deliverable 2 — consolidated cross-domain tooling/stack inventory (PC/local dev, Data/MySQL, AWS/V3.0 backend, Google Play, runtimes) — assemble + confirm from the actual environment + docs, not memory. Feeds the shared-layer language decision.
iPad open items
  iPad mesh source: A (bridge/port-listener) vs B (fork Meshtastic-Apple).
  Service layer: local-on-device vs network vs both.
  Shared-layer language/runtime (Kotlin/KMP leading, since logic is already Kotlin).
  Reconcile Meshtastic-Apple's native TAK/CoT vs the roadmap's "TAK as pattern only."
  Confirm the Meshtastic backup/restore file format + cross-platform acceptance.
iPad EVOLUTION — how the thinking got here (the 4 prior positions) HISTORY
The iPad plan evolved four times before 07-04 reconciled it. Kept so the ground isn't re-walked:
  (1) Roadmap V9 (Mar 25): native-port via external dev.
  (2) Mar-14 discussion doc — staged Options A–D: (A) fork Meshtastic-Apple in Swift/SwiftUI (rated HIGH, needs Swift skills); (B) React Native/Flutter (LOW — explicitly excluded); (C) WKWebView hybrid reusing convoy_map.html + minimal Swift BLE bridge (MEDIUM, ~2-3 wk); (D) use unmodified Meshtastic-Apple as a display-only viewer (HIGH for viewing, LOW for full convoy). Recommended: D short-term → C (V3) → A (V4). Also recommended MapLibre GL + PMTiles/OpenMapTiles for offline, replacing Leaflet.
  (3) May notes: PWA-via-Bluefy-then-Capacitor.
  (4) Repeatedly flagged "iPad V2.5 vs V3.0, not resolved."
What 07-04 overturned: MapLibre + PMTiles DROPPED (V2.6 tile design went MBTiles-only, PMTiles rejected as immutable, stayed on Leaflet not MapLibre). The A/B/C/D ladder collapsed — since presentation is already web, the WKWebView shell is the presentation host in BOTH remaining candidates, and the open decision narrowed to A (fork) vs a bridge/port-listener for the MESH SOURCE, not a 4-option choice; SwiftUI rejected for presentation. iPad moved from "V4, viewer-only short-term" to "the post-V2.6 target," sequenced through KMP + Mac-first. Several Mar-14 open questions now answered: tile area = ½mi-padded bbox (track) / drawn bbox (area); download at ride/track creation under the app's own entitlement; same architectural relationship as Android (fork). ATAK/CoT-as-pattern-only still holds (mesh replaces the server; protobuf replaces CoT-over-UDP).
V3.0 — SERVER / SHARING / DISTRIBUTION
Standing awareness. Gated on real entitlement AND revenue.
V3.0 track/ride sharing rules STRATEGY
  LOCAL = preferred name. UNIVERSAL/AWS = first-in for hash sets the canonical name; first-in for (hash,date) sets an alias. Group-ride collapse needs fuzzy/spatial matching. AWS import = stage-to-dir + reuse the local import path.
  Open design problem: same-ride cross-device matching (unsolved).
  Tile redistribution (deferred from V2.6): operator-side rehosting = redistribution = V3.0, gated on real entitlement AND revenue. The licensing line = intent-to-redistribute / who-hosts, not processed-vs-unprocessed. V2.6 = method change only, each client fetches under the app's own entitlement; AWS/Box holds a manifest (tract→extent→hash), not tile bytes. Safe-now AWS alternative: public-domain gov tiles (USGS/USFS/BLM).

REFERENCE (durable — always-loaded)
Track model + data-integrity architecture (locked) LOCKED
  SPATIAL tables PURE OGC; properties/surveys/aliases/queues in the EXTENSION db (grouptrack_data.db) by id. Separate SQLite files — NO cross-DB JOIN. Boundary change = stop-and-check. (Note: the tile MBTiles files are ALSO separate per-type SQLite DBs — the DB rules engine's reach over them vs only the GPX/track DBs is a tile Step-0 scope question.)
  tracks: track_id PK, name, bbox, timestamps, geometry, min/max lat/lon, type, geom_hash NOT NULL UNIQUE (SHA-256 of WKT). track_properties: track_id PK, filename UNIQUE, source_format, recorded_at, distance_miles, duration_minutes, max/avg_speed_mph, elevation_gain_ft, point_count, shared, ride_id, area_id. artifact_aliases: alias_id, artifact_type (SINGULAR), artifact_id, alias, is_preferred (LOCAL), source, geom_hash.
  Storage: my_tracks GPX (/sdcard/Documents/my_tracks) = SOURCE OF TRUTH; DBs + receipt at /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/; tiles at /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/maps today (→ MBTiles-only per-type hard cutover = V2.6 tile ITEM A; install/update will STOP creating maps). Track files &lt;track_id&gt;.gpx. DELETE-AND-RESYNC off the table for deletes; forced resync on install = additive rebuild-from-source. Recorder GPX = lat/lon/ele/time only, NO &lt;speed&gt;, 3s sampling (→ 2s change-gated V2.6).
  "Artifact builds, not process builds": complete tracks fully, test as a unit, THEN routes, THEN waypoints.

18 (07-04) SCOUR THE CORPUS BEFORE PLANNING — read the docs' full evolution + reasons before offering a view; summaries are a lossy index; partner not new-employee. · 19 (07-05) DESTRUCTIVE ops rank by BLAST RADIUS not speed — surgical-slow &gt; fast-total; MBTiles = surgical+instant. STATE over inference (explicit recorded mode &gt; disk side-effects, resolved at app open). · 20 (07-06) REUSE + FIND THE EXISTING BLACK BOX BEFORE DESIGNING — funnel into the existing proven component (area submission, fit process, one write contract, provider's own unpack, DB rules engine); for any unknown, find the existing component + verify against memory before designing; capture the BLAST RADIUS so a change doesn't underestimate what it breaks. · 21 (07-06) DOC PROCESS — write detail INTO this living doc (collapsible), generate at EOD, paste into GroupTrack docs → AllDocs; memory alone doesn't reach AllDocs and referenced external files can vanish.

        Trail data has been assembled from a trusted group of public authorities. Some groups are regional or state-specific. Others are nationwide.

        By source — Import by the source owner: Utah, USFS, BLM, and others.

function goTo(n) {
  document.querySelectorAll('.screen').forEach(s => s.classList.remove('active'));
  document.getElementById('s'+n).classList.add('active');
}

(function(){
  var mode='Area';
  var data={Area:['Cedar City, UT','Cedar City Regional, UT','Cedar Fort, UT'],
            Track:['Cedar City to Newcastle','Old Irontown loop'],
            Route:['Sunday Desert Run'],
            Trail:['13th Hole','13th Hole','Jordan River Trail','Gooseberry Mesa'],
            Waypoint:['Gooseberry Trailhead','Water cache']};
  var $=function(id){return document.getElementById(id)};
  function step(t){$('step').textContent=t}
  function paint(){[].forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('.chip'),function(c){
    c.classList.toggle('on',c.dataset.m===mode)});
    $('q').placeholder=mode==='Area'?'Search area (e.g. Cedar City)\u2026':'Search '+mode.toLowerCase()+' by name\u2026'}
  function openBar(){$('bar').classList.remove('hidden');$('list').classList.add('hidden');
    $('detail').classList.add('hidden');$('mapNote').textContent='';$('q').value='';$('q').focus();step('2 · pick type + type, enter')}
  function run(){$('bar').classList.add('hidden');step('3 · pick from matches');
    var items=data[mode]||[],seen={};
    $('rhead').textContent=items.length+' '+(mode==='Area'?'place':mode.toLowerCase())+' match'+(items.length===1?'':'es');
    $('rows').innerHTML=items.map(function(n){seen[n]=(seen[n]||0)+1;
      var dup=items.filter(function(x){return x===n}).length>1;
      var seq=dup?' #'+seen[n]+'':'';
      return ''+(mode==='Area'?'\u25C9 ':'\u203A ')+n+seq+''}).join('');
    $('list').classList.remove('hidden');
    [].forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('.row'),function(b){b.onclick=function(){pick(b.dataset.n)}})}
  function pick(name){$('list').classList.add('hidden');
    if(mode==='Area'){$('mapNote').textContent='\u25CE centered on '+name;step('done · map recentered')}
    else{$('dName').textContent=name;$('dType').textContent=mode.toUpperCase();
      $('detail').classList.remove('hidden');step('done · detail open (FIT here)')}}
  $('fab').onclick=openBar;
  $('barX').onclick=function(){$('bar').classList.add('hidden');step('1 · tap the beacon')};
  $('dX').onclick=function(){$('detail').classList.add('hidden')};
  [].forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('.chip'),function(c){c.onclick=function(){mode=c.dataset.m;paint()}});
  $('q').addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Enter')run()});
  $('reset').onclick=function(){$('bar').classList.add('hidden');$('list').classList.add('hidden');
    $('detail').classList.add('hidden');$('mapNote').textContent='';mode='Area';paint();step('1 · tap the beacon')};
  paint();
})();

⛔ Open tasks — UI data (finish these first; they complete the UI)
  Open · pick up first
  1 · FIT SEL/EDIT-panel row update (the one remaining FIT piece)
  Decision already made — implement Option B. No re-diagnosis needed.
    Symptom: FIT applies correctly (centers, selects, JSON perfect) but the SEL/EDIT panel is still open underneath. When that panel later closes, its launch-time state (all / none) takes precedence and overrides the FIT — the trail disappears or all artifacts show.
    Why: FIT never writes the panel's row state. A manual row-select writes it (proven: manually selecting the same row you just fitted works); FIT does not. The viewport query always runs and applies off/on/selected — FIT just never sets the panel row to SELECTED + the fitted id.
    Fix (Option B, chosen because it removes any user-interaction path that can break FIT state): on FIT / detail launch, close the SEL/EDIT panel and set its row + state to the one fitted artifact — i.e. selectedArtifactIds = setOf(fittedId) and activeListType = fittedType, plus showArtifactsPanel = false.
    Where: ConvoyScreen onOpenDetail ~line 1292 and ~1780 (both set pendingDetail* but never close the panel). Mirror the manual-select row write found in commit 35ccccc4a ~lines 1678-1679 (selectedArtifactIds = …; activeListType = typeName). Apply to both screens.
  Open
  2 · Widen artifact selection radius on the map (touch tolerance)
    Both map HTMLs use the default SVG renderer. Add renderer: L.svg({ tolerance: 12 }) to the L.map(...) call — one line per HTML (convoy_map.html and grouptrack_map.html). Widens the hit zone for all artifact taps. Tunable 12 → 15–18.
    Independent, low risk. Part of the "simple JS selection focus" change.
  Open
  3 · Trail info panel — display real data from the extension DB
    Current state: the map-tap popup shows "Unknown" for Surface / Uses / CartoCode. The map retrieve (queryTrailsByViewport → buildTrailGeoJson) reads only the spatial DB, where those property columns are blank. The real values (including carto_code) live in the extension DB trail_properties and are never retrieved by the map path.
    Approach (Fred's, additive — NOT a rewrite): after the existing spatial retrieve, additionally pull the wanted fields from trail_properties and emit them into the popup. Color the whole CartoCode line by carto code (mirror the 8-color cartoStyle in JS), trails only.
    Do not rewrite the working spatial retrieve; layer the extension lookup on top as a second step.
  Open · regression (new today)
  4 · Track arrows display when they shouldn't
    Symptom (new today, never before): track directional arrows still display when tracks are OFF, or when only one track is SELECTED. Arrows should show only when tracks show.
    convoy_map.html was not in today's commits, so the regression is either in how the Kotlin side calls track show/hide/update, or the arrow layer not being removed on hide.
    Next: read convoy_map.html ~lines 448–495 (trackArrows = L.polylineDecorator, showTracks/hideTracks/updateTracks). Confirm hideTracks removes trackArrows, and that updateTracks rebuilds arrows honoring the SELECTED filter (not all tracks). Not yet root-caused.

function showScreen(id) {
  document.querySelectorAll('.screen').forEach(s => s.classList.remove('active'));
  document.querySelectorAll('.nav-tab').forEach(t => t.classList.remove('active'));
  document.getElementById(id).classList.add('active');
  event.target.classList.add('active');
}
function showPanel(id) {
  // Hide all panels in current screen except display
  const screen = document.querySelector('.screen.active');
  screen.querySelectorAll('.panel').forEach(p => p.classList.remove('visible'));
  document.getElementById(id).classList.add('visible');
}
function hidePanel(id) {
  document.getElementById(id).classList.remove('visible');
}
function togglePanel(id) {
  document.getElementById(id).classList.toggle('visible');
}
function toggle(id) {
  const el = document.getElementById(id);
  el.style.display = el.style.display === 'none' ? 'block' : 'none';
}
function toggleAccordion(header) {
  const body = header.nextElementSibling;
  body.classList.toggle('open');
  const arrow = header.querySelector('span:last-child');
  arrow.textContent = body.classList.contains('open') ? 'v' : '>';
}
function setHud(mode) {
  // Hide all HUDs
  document.querySelectorAll('.hud-strip').forEach(h => h.classList.remove('visible'));
  document.querySelectorAll('.hud-btn').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
  hidePanel('c-cart-picker');
  if (mode === 'group') {
    document.getElementById('c-hud-group').classList.add('visible');
    document.getElementById('c-btn-group').classList.add('active');
  } else if (mode === 'mycart') {
    document.getElementById('c-hud-mycart').classList.add('visible');
    document.getElementById('c-btn-mycart').classList.add('active');
  } else if (mode === 'node') {
    document.getElementById('c-hud-node').classList.add('visible');
    document.getElementById('c-btn-select').classList.add('active');
  } else if (mode === 'hide') {
    document.getElementById('c-btn-hide').classList.add('active');
  }
}

E3. WRITE-FUNCTION DATA CONTRACT (so in-progress JSON mirrors it)
The completed-save consumes the RouteManager VERTEX chain (the only true source of shape). Each Vertex: lat, lon, lineId(String?), lineType(String?), segmentIndex(Int, -1 if free), t(Double 0..1), snapped(Boolean). It produces wkt + bbox via buildWktAndBbox and writes insertRoute(name,wkt,bbox...). The completed DB row stores ONLY wkt+bbox+name (resolved geometry) — it throws away HOW the route was built.
The DRAFT (in-progress) JSON must NOT throw that away — it stores the FULL vertex list so resume = true editing (undo to a snapped vertex, know which legs ride a trail, re-slice), not redrawing a frozen line. wkt is always re-derivable from vertices; the reverse is not. Draft schema (future build):
{ schemaVersion, draftId, name|null, createdAt, updatedAt, method,
  vertices:[ {lat,lon,lineId|null,lineType|null,segmentIndex,t,snapped}, ... ] }
  // NO wkt/bbox in draft — DERIVED at graduation by replaying buildWktAndBbox.
RESUME = parse → addVertex(Vertex(...)) each → drawBuildLine. GRADUATE = identical Build-1 onSaveCompleted path + delete draft JSON. The ONLY writes ever: create draft JSON (Save in-progress) · overwrite draft JSON (Save with changes) · insertRoute+delete-draft (Save as completed, graduation). A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row, never both.
E4. ENGINE FRAMING (route creation is its OWN complex birth process)
STATES: Route(base) → New → In Progress → Completed. ACTIVITIES: Save, Discard (drive transitions). CONDITIONS: ≥2 pts? · new vs resumed · draft-on-disk? · delete-saved=NO · resave=YES may ALIAS per §K/§L. ACTIONS (reusable black boxes, params+execute): JSON write/open/delete · spatial-DB add/update/delete. Everything in-memory until deliberate Save. Each artifact has its OWN creation process — route is the COMPLEX one (heavy human contact); importing a trail / dropping a waypoint / recording a track are different. Completed tracks have their own lifecycle too (later).

E3. WRITE-FUNCTION DATA CONTRACT (in-progress JSON mirrors it)
Completed-save consumes the RouteManager VERTEX chain (only true source of shape). Vertex: lat, lon, lineId(String?), lineType(String?), segmentIndex(Int,-1 free), t(0..1), snapped(Bool). Produces wkt+bbox → insertRoute. Completed DB row stores ONLY wkt+bbox+name — throws away HOW it was built.
DRAFT JSON must NOT — stores the FULL vertex list so resume = true editing (undo to a snapped vertex, know which legs ride a trail, re-slice), not a frozen line. wkt re-derivable from vertices; reverse not. Schema (future):
{ schemaVersion, draftId, name|null, createdAt, updatedAt, method,
  vertices:[ {lat,lon,lineId|null,lineType|null,segmentIndex,t,snapped}, ... ] }
  // NO wkt/bbox — DERIVED at graduation by replaying buildWktAndBbox.
RESUME = parse → addVertex each → drawBuildLine. GRADUATE = identical Build-1 save path + delete draft. ONLY writes ever: create draft JSON · overwrite draft JSON · insertRoute+delete-draft. A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row, never both.
E4. ENGINE FRAMING
STATES: Route(base)→New→In Progress→Completed. ACTIVITIES: Save, Discard. CONDITIONS: ≥2 pts? · new vs resumed · draft-on-disk? · delete-saved=NO · resave=YES may ALIAS (§K/§L). ACTIONS (black boxes, params+execute): JSON write/open/delete · spatial-DB add/update/delete. In-memory until deliberate Save. Each artifact has its OWN birth process — route is the COMPLEX one; trail-import / waypoint-drop / track-record differ. Completed tracks have their own lifecycle (later).

E3. WRITE-FUNCTION DATA CONTRACT
Completed-save consumes the RouteManager VERTEX chain. Vertex: lat, lon, lineId(String?), lineType(String?), segmentIndex(-1 free), t(0..1), snapped(Bool). Completed DB row stores ONLY wkt+bbox+name. DRAFT JSON stores the FULL vertex list (resume = true editing). Schema: {schemaVersion, draftId, name|null, createdAt, updatedAt, method, vertices:[{lat,lon,lineId|null,lineType|null,segmentIndex,t,snapped}]} — NO wkt/bbox (derived at graduation). RESUME = parse→addVertex→drawBuildLine. GRADUATE = Build-1 save path + delete draft. A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row.
E4. ENGINE FRAMING
STATES: Route→New→In Progress→Completed. ACTIVITIES: Save, Discard. CONDITIONS: ≥2 pts? · new vs resumed · draft-on-disk? · delete-saved=NO · resave may ALIAS (§K/§L). Each artifact has its OWN birth process — route is the complex one.
E5. SHARED TABLE RULE (folded from Decision Log §4.4/4.6, rules 32-33)
Tracks and routes share ONE table with a TYPE field (TRACK/ROUTE). "All imports are TRACKS, always. Convert-to-route is an explicit, REVERSIBLE type flip." source_track_id links a converted track to its route. Implication for snap-2: our insertRoute writes a row of type ROUTE in that shared table; route dedup therefore rides the same geom_hash/UNIQUE machinery as tracks (§K). Route delete is BLOCKED if type=ROUTE and assigned to an active ride with enrollments (V3.0 concern, not 2.5). Identity = geometry; display names in aliases.

P. Data Protection — backup / journal / rollback (deferred V2.5 schema spec)
Deferred (schema-hardening subsystem, not snap-2). Full spec: GroupTrack_V25_DataProtection_v1 (archived). Three layers on grouptrack_user.spatialite: (1) Backup — auto on launch + before destructive ops; last 5 retained; /Documents/GroupTrack/data/backups/. (2) Change journal — every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on user tables (waypoints/routes/tracks/ride_areas), before+after state as JSON, geometry as WKT, 12 triggers, 30-day retention. (3) Rollback — single-op undo, transaction rollback, point-in-time; creates backup first. Relevance to routes: when route create/edit/delete is journaled, the before/after must store geometry as WKT (matches our write-contract's vertex→wkt derivation). NOT journaled: trail data (re-downloadable), transfer queue. Rules 23-25.

E3. ROUTE LIFECYCLE — SETTLED MODEL (Item 1 — ready to build)
Full spec: RouteLifecycle_SETTLED_DESIGN_2026-06-05. Reflects all 2026-06-05 simplifications.
Core rules:
R1 Either/or — a route is EITHER an in-progress draft (JSON) OR a completed DB row, never both; graduation writes the row + deletes the draft.
R2 Identity — in-progress identity = the typed NAME (set at New); route id assigned ONLY at graduation under DB dedup rules.
R3 Save exits — every save EXITS route mode; to continue editing, Save In Progress then RE-SELECT from the In-Progress list. NO mid-session "save &amp; continue", NO in-place state promotion.
R4 State fixed at launch — New ⇒ NEW whole session; Select In-Progress ⇒ RESUMED whole session. The entry row is the launch fork that sets the state the adaptive screens read.
R5 Writes minimal — only create-draft, overwrite-draft, insertRoute(+delete-draft), delete-draft. Roll-back / discard-new / cancel NEVER write.
R6 Both maps — ConvoyScreen (LF) + ConvoyMapViewerScreen (CRLF), shared RouteManager; toolbar CRLF; cat -A before every patch.
R7 Vertices not wkt — draft stores the full vertex chain; wkt/bbox derived at graduation (resumed draft graduates through the IDENTICAL completed-save path).
Save/Discard placement: on the COLLAPSED title bar (one-tap access, no real-estate cost) AND in the expanded panel. Each is ONE entry point opening an adaptive SCREEN; choices driven by fixed launch state.
Adaptive SAVE screen — NEW: [Save completed (≥2 pts, LIVE)] · [Save in-progress → writeDraft, exit (SOON)] · [Cancel]. RESUMED: [Graduate (+deleteDraft) (SOON)] · [Save with changes → overwriteDraft, exit (SOON)] · [Cancel].
Adaptive DISCARD screen — NEW: [Discard &amp; exit (LIVE, no write)] · [Keep building]. RESUMED: [Roll back = reload unchanged draft, no write (SOON)] · [Delete in-progress = deleteDraft (SOON)] · [Keep building].
Add ↔ Method coupling (CONFIRMED): Add is DEFAULT GREEN/on entering BOTH New and In-Progress. ASYMMETRIC — turns OFF/RED ONLY when Draw or Suggest is selected (no manual turn-off); the ONLY manual action is tapping Add to turn it back ON, reclaiming control from Draw/Suggest. Add = "design-control-is-here" indicator, NOT a free toggle.
SOON — Patch 1 (UI-first) routeState (NEW|RESUMED + name) · adaptive Save/Discard SCREENS · Save/Discard on collapsed bar · EMULATED Select-In-Progress (hardcoded list + vertex chain). All store calls STUBBED (log). Files: ConvoyRouteToolbar (CRLF) + ConvoyScreen (LF) + ConvoyMapViewerScreen (CRLF). Walk the ✓-stub checklist rows on BOTH maps.
SOON — Patch 2 Real RouteDraftStore.kt (Context-holding; RouteManager stays pure): writeDraft(name,vertices,method) · overwriteDraft · listDrafts→[{name,updatedAt,pointCount}] · openDraft(name)→{vertices,method} (resume AND roll-back) · deleteDraft(name). Storage /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/route_drafts/&lt;name&gt;.json; atomic temp+rename. JSON {schemaVersion,name,createdAt,updatedAt,method,vertices[…]} — no id, no wkt. Swap stubs for real calls; verify round-trip via logcat.
SOON — Patch 3 Wire graduate-delete + Discard-delete + roll-back-reload to real store. Full end-to-end, both maps.
OPEN — decide before functions (a) duplicate-name policy for drafts (block / overwrite / disambiguate-file); (b) Discard-on-NEW acts directly vs confirm prompt; (c) In-Progress over-limit threshold if any.
E4. WRITE-FUNCTION DATA CONTRACT
Completed-save consumes the RouteManager VERTEX chain. Vertex: lat, lon, lineId(String?), lineType(String?), segmentIndex(-1 free), t(0..1), snapped(Bool). Completed DB row stores ONLY wkt+bbox+name. DRAFT JSON stores the FULL vertex list (resume = true editing), NOT wkt. RESUME = parse→addVertex→drawBuildLine. GRADUATE = Build-1 save path + delete draft. A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row. Full spec: RouteWriteFunction_DataContract_2026-06-04.
E5. SHARED TABLE RULE
Tracks + routes share ONE table with a TYPE field (TRACK/ROUTE). insertRoute writes type=ROUTE; route dedup rides the same geom_hash/UNIQUE machinery as tracks (§K add-core bypass). Convert-to-route = reversible type flip; source_track_id links a converted track to its route. Route delete BLOCKED if type=ROUTE and assigned to an active ride with enrollments (V3.0 concern, not 2.5).
E6. FILE-ENDING FACTS
ConvoyScreen.kt = LF · ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt = CRLF · ConvoyRouteToolbar.kt = CRLF (flipped this session; future toolbar patches MUST be CRLF). cat -A before every patch. Route mode is a TWO-FILE MIRROR (screens) + toolbar.

O. Standing Rules (pointer — full list in archived docs)
54 numbered Standing Rules live in MasterPlan + Decision Log (May 17), archived. Highlights: 1 never auto-delete user data (explicit confirm) · 2 never embed API keys · 3 share opt-in only · 4 offline-first · 26 schema hardened before app code · 28 patch scripts uniquely versioned · 29 never commit V3_FEATURES_ENABLED/V25_SPATIAL_ENABLED=true · 30 preserve full trail geometry precision (snap-to depends on it) · 31 impact analysis before ANY change · 32-33 all imports are tracks; tracks/routes share table · 43 NO MediaStore queries · 54 one comprehensive patch per agreed design. Full text: search Drive "MasterPlan" / "DecisionLog".
P. Data Protection — backup / journal / rollback (deferred V2.5 schema spec)
Deferred (schema-hardening subsystem, not snap-2). Full spec: GroupTrack_V25_DataProtection_v1 (archived). Three layers on grouptrack_user.spatialite: (1) Backup — auto on launch + before destructive ops; last 5 retained; /Documents/GroupTrack/data/backups/. (2) Change journal — every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on user tables, before+after as JSON, geometry as WKT, 12 triggers, 30-day retention. (3) Rollback — single-op undo, transaction rollback, point-in-time; creates backup first. Relevance to routes: when route create/edit/delete is journaled, before/after stores geometry as WKT (matches the write-contract's vertex→wkt derivation). NOT journaled: trail data (re-downloadable), transfer queue. Rules 23-25.

B. Snap-2 — CONVOY MAP: DONE &amp; PROVEN ON DEVICE
  WIN Snap-2 now traces the route along trail/track geometry on the convoy map (ConvoyScreen.kt). Confirmed three ways: logcat (tracedLen grows far faster than vertex count as consecutive same-line snapped points fill in trail geometry — one run snapped 5→6 jumped tracedLen 709→2802 = a long trail slice; the pts= arrays contain intermediate trail vertices, not just taps), on-screen, and reproduced via undo/repost.
  What was wrong &amp; what fixed it
    Confirmed (branch A): snap COMPUTES &amp; STORES correctly. Draft JSON had vertices with "snapped":true, real lineId, lineType, segmentIndex, interpolation t. buildSegments() (RouteManager.kt:218) genuinely traces — walks consecutive pairs, sameLine = a.snapped &amp;&amp; b.snapped &amp;&amp; same lineId, slices the underlying line via sliceLine using pos=segmentIndex+t. Its ONLY caller was buildWktAndBbox (save-completed) — the draw paths bypassed it.
    Fix: the live draw now runs the snapped vertices through buildSegments against the viewport geometry, swaps [lon,lat]→[lat,lon], and feeds drawBuildLine. Patched block: addVertex(v); val pts = withContext(IO){ init; queryTrails+TracksByViewport; byId(trail_id/track_id→geometry); buildSegments{ lineId→byId[lineId]?.let{ parseWktLine } }.joinToString swap [lat,lon] }; drawBuildLine(pts).
    TWO handlers, both patched: ConvoyScreen has two onMapTap — site 544 in the if(existing != null) persistent-WebView branch, and site 694 in the else/factory branch. Fresh map sessions run the FACTORY (694) handler — patching 544 alone did nothing visible; the 694 patch is what made it work. (Recurring "two handlers" trap.) Patches: patch_v25_trailtrace_site1_544_v6.py, patch_v25_trailtrace_site2_694_v1.py.
  Behavior notes (not bugs)
    Snap catch-rate depends on ZOOM — radius is hardcoded 30.0 m real-world; zoomed out (~¼ mile) almost nothing snaps, zoomed in it catches reliably.
    Trace only draws between TWO CONSECUTIVE snapped vertices on the SAME line — isolated or cross-line snapped points draw straight to their neighbors, by design.
  Diagnostic logs retained in committed code: tracedLen at ConvoyScreen ~555 and S2 tracedLen at ~716. Harmless Log.d; strip at AAB prep (see §E).
C. Snap-2 + Undo — PLANNING MAP: NEXT (must work before AAB)
  NEXT ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt is the PLANNING map. Solving the convoy map did NOT solve this — separate onMapTap + draw per file (shared RouteManager/SpatialDbManager, separate display). TWO problems:
  C-1 · Snap-2 trace not working on planning map
    All planning-map draw sites still use RAW routeVertices().joinToString chords: 498 (onMapTap live), 982 (undo redraw), 1040 (rollback rbPts), 1075 (resume rsPts — call is setRouteMode(true); drawBuildLine(...)).
    Fix: mirror the convoy-map trace (withContext IO → query viewport → byId → buildSegments → swap → drawBuildLine) to these sites. Per-file indentation differs (dialogs nest deeper here). Confirm endings via raw Python rb read before patching (see §D).
  C-2 · Undo does not remove segments on planning map
    Undo handler at 981–983 LOOKS correct: RouteManager.undoVertex() → rebuild pts → redraw. Resume at 1072 DOES call RouteDraftStore.loadIntoRouteManager(d) (which clearRoute() + addVertex per vertex), so the builder list IS populated on resume — so "empty vertices" is NOT the obvious cause.
    MIXED SIGNALS to resolve first: Fred reported undo "does not remove segments" on a resumed in-progress route (opened with all its points), but ALSO that undo "works on new trails." RE-TEST cleanly next session: (1) New route on planning map → tap → undo (works?). (2) Resume a draft → undo (works?). That fork tells us undo-broken-generally vs undo-broken-only-after-resume.
    If it no-ops even on a new route: instrument the undo handler (981) to log routeVertices().size before/after — confirms whether undoVertex() fires and whether the planning map is touching the same RouteManager state its taps build into.
D. File / build facts (current, verified tonight)
    LINE ENDINGS — TRAP: ConvoyScreen.kt has MIXED endings. file reports CRLF (majority); some lines are LF. cat -A, grep -U, and xxd piped through sed all LIE (sed normalizes the ending → shows LF on a CRLF line). The ONLY reliable check is a raw Python byte read:
      python3 -c "d=open(PATH,'rb').read(); i=d.find(b'&lt;anchor&gt;'); print(repr(d[i-260:i+115]))"
      Line 544's draw line actually ends \r\n. Write patch OLD/NEW with \r\n to match. No BOM (first bytes = pac of package).
    Identical lines repeat across sites (the raw pts line at 544 == 694) → single-line anchors match 2×. Fold in unique context above (the freeVertex/addVertex lines, or the 36-space vs 32-space indent) to disambiguate.
    RouteManager.kt + SpatialDbManager.kt + RouteDraftStore.kt are LF. Column = androidx.compose.foundation.layout.
    Viewport query keys (verified live): queryTrailsByViewport → trail_id,name,geometry; queryTracksByViewport → track_id,name,geometry. geometry = WKT. parseWktLine handles LINESTRING/MULTILINESTRING "lon lat".
    Commit with explicit file lists, not git add -A. Build ~11–21 min incremental.
    Recovery anchor (from Decision Log): commit 204405fc7 "snap-2 clean base: factory onMapTap snaps radius 30; buildable rollback point." Fallback AAB at versionCode 29320600 already on Play Internal as the safety net.
E. AAB milestone — GATED on §C
  GATE AAB only after BOTH planning-map undo AND planning-map snap-2 trace are confirmed working.
    STRIP diagnostic logs first — ConvoyScreen tracedLen (~555) + S2 tracedLen (~716) + any added to the planning map. Release build should carry no debug Log.d.
    Then: bump versionCode (Droid builds seen to 29320598; fallback AAB was 29320600), confirm signing, fix SpecifyForegroundServiceType in AndroidManifest, bundleGoogleRelease, docs in sync, upload.
    PRE-AAB carry-over: verify streaming-parser geometry not OVER-capturing (feeds map draw, route snapping, AWS sync).
F. Parked (captured, not active)
    PARK Snap radius slider (Fred's original design): 80 m default + in-app slider so radius is tunable without recompiling. GroupTrack — User Manual (V2.5)
Cookbook style. Each section is one screen; every function on that screen is documented in place. The ? help icon on a screen deep-links to that screen's section here.
V2.5 · 2026-06-18 · Online edition: grouptrack.org/manual · Bundled offline copy ships in-app · Sections map 1:1 to the screens that carry a ? help icon.
How help links work: tapping ? on a screen opens this manual at that screen's section (the anchors below — #planning-map, #convoy-map, #radio-write, #artifacts). V2.5 scope for the ? icon: the screens that persist into 3.0 — Planning Map, Convoy Map (incl. the Meshtastic connection/monitoring panel), and the Convoy radio-write menu. The goal in 3.0 is ? on every screen.
Sections
1. Planning Map — explore trails, build routes, import/manage artifacts off-radio
2. Convoy Map — live group tracking + Meshtastic connection &amp; monitoring panel
3. Convoy Radio-Write Menu — apply / archive / restore radio config transitional, supported in V2.5
4. Work with Artifacts — trails, tracks, waypoints, routes (display, select/edit, create)
1 · Planning Map
Screen: Planning Map · ? help anchor: #planning-map
The Planning Map is the off-radio workspace: explore downloaded trails, import your track history, build and save routes, and manage what's displayed — all without a radio connected. It shares the spatial database and route engine with the Convoy Map, but keeps its own display state.
Map basics
Pan / zoom: drag to pan, pinch to zoom. These stay live at all times, even while building a route.
Base layers (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+): switch imagery from the layer control. Tiles are served from your offline cache when available.
Viewport-aware display: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes load for the area you're viewing. Zoom in to see more detail; the display fills in as you move.
Displaying trails, tracks, waypoints, routes
See Section 4 (Work with Artifacts) — the toggle/select/edit controls are shared and documented there.
Too many trails in view: if the current view contains more trails than can be displayed at once, the SEL/Edit control indicates "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." Zoom in to narrow the area until trails become selectable. guidance behavior — coming
Building a route
See the full cookbook entry in Section 4 → Creating a Route. Route building works identically on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Importing trails / tracks
Import tracks (GPX): bring in your recorded track history. Large files import via streaming; duplicates (same geometry) are skipped automatically, and a recap shows new vs. already-in-library.
Import trails by area: draw an area to list and download trail sources overlapping it. processing fix in progress
Coming: waypoint and route extraction from GPX (all GPX imports are currently treated as tracks); GPX/KML open-with handler.
2 · Convoy Map
Screen: Convoy Map (incl. Meshtastic connection / monitoring panel) · ? help anchor: #convoy-map
The Convoy Map is the live group-tracking screen used during a ride. It shows your position and the positions of other riders relayed over the Meshtastic LoRa mesh, plus the same trail/track/waypoint/route display and route-building tools as the Planning Map.
Connecting to your radio (connection &amp; monitoring panel)
Connect: open the connection panel and pair your Meshtastic device (e.g. T1000-E) over Bluetooth. The panel shows connection state.
Monitoring: the panel reports link status and node activity. Use it to confirm the mesh is up before relying on positions.
Device compatibility: some budget Android devices cannot hold a stable Bluetooth link to the radio (the connection drops after several seconds). If positions stop updating and the panel shows repeated disconnects, the device may be incompatible — see the tester compatibility list.
Live tracking
Rider positions: other riders appear as node markers, updated as mesh packets arrive.
Your position: driven by the phone GPS once location permission is granted.
Waypoints
Drop a waypoint: long-press the map to drop a waypoint pin.
Pin shape: waypoints display as teardrop pins — the pin's point marks the exact location you dropped it. Each waypoint type has its own color and icon.
Proximity: waypoints within 100 m are treated as the same location.
Help on this screen
? help: tap the ? button on the Convoy Map to open the release notes or the full user manual. (The same help is on the Planning Map; both open the same documents.)
Download QUEUES (tile downloads)
QUEUES: opens the live download monitor (top-right) showing tile-download progress.
Building a route on the Convoy Map
Identical to the Planning Map — see Section 4 → Creating a Route.
3 · Convoy Radio-Write Menu (Apply / Archive / Restore)
Screen: Convoy menu — radio configuration · ? help anchor: #radio-write
Transitional — current and supported in V2.5. These radio-configuration functions are how radio writes happen this release. They are slated to be replaced in 3.0, but they work now and you should use them. This manual fully covers them; the 3.0 manual will rewrite this section when the functions change.
Apply Convoy Config (write to radio)
Connect the radio first (Section 2 connection panel) — the write action is unavailable with no Bluetooth link.
Open the Convoy menu → radio configuration.
Review the config values (channel, encryption keys, device settings). Values are validated before writing.
Apply. The write proceeds screen-by-screen / in passes through the config groups; confirm each completes.
Field validation: the config is validated (e.g. full field check) before programming. A two-pass programming approach is used so all config groups are written and confirmed.
Archive radio config
Save the current working radio configuration so it can be restored later. Use this before making changes.
Restore radio config
Re-apply a previously archived configuration to the connected radio.
Coming (replaces this menu in a future build): a screen-by-screen radio-config writer that mirrors each Meshtastic config screen, pre-populated and read-only, with a PROCEED button that is disabled (red) until the radio is connected (then green), saving after each screen through all config groups.
4 · Work with Artifacts
Screen: Work with Artifacts (shared by both maps)
"Work with Artifacts" is the control center for everything you display and create on the map: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes. The toggle and select/edit controls are the same on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Display toggles (ON / OFF / SELECTED)
ON: show all artifacts of that type in view.
OFF: hide that type.
SELECTED: show only the items you've checked in that type's select/edit list.
Select / Edit list (per type)
Open a type's SEL/Edit list to check individual items for SELECTED display, or to open an item's detail.
Search by name: choose an artifact type, type a name, and press Enter to find matching trails, tracks, waypoints, or routes by name across your whole database (not just what's on screen). Search is case-insensitive and matches partial names. Tap a result to open its detail. new in this build
Item detail: tapping an item's name (from a search result or the select/edit list) opens its detail card. The left side lists the actions available for that item's type; the right side shows the item's information. For trails this includes designated uses, surface type, classification (carto code), county, managing agency, and data source. Less-used technical values — bounding coordinates, created/updated dates, and the geometry hash — are tucked under a ▸ technical toggle so the useful information shows first; tap it to expand. Where a trail has alternate names on record, they appear here too. On the Convoy Map the detail is view-only; full editing is on the Planning Map.
FIT (fit to map): from an item's detail card, tap FIT to frame that item on the map. The map flies to the item and zooms to fit it, the item is selected and drawn on its own, and the other artifact types are turned off — so you see just the one you picked. Works for trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes, on both maps. FIT is how you go from finding a name to seeing it on the map.
List limit: the list currently shows up to 200 items. paging — coming
Trails over-limit: when more trails are in view than can be shown, SEL/Edit shows "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." coming
Track display
Tracks display as dashed green lines from your device's spatial database. When Tracks are on, each track shows direction-of-travel arrows along the line so you can read which way it runs — useful for telling a single looping track from two overlapping ones. The arrows are evenly spaced on screen and stay readable as you zoom, and are drawn in the same neon green as the track.
Routes display
Routes display as magenta lines, loaded from your device's spatial database the same viewport-aware way as trails and tracks. Build a route with + ROUTE (see Creating a Route). (Importing routes from GPX, and the Draw / Suggest build methods, are coming in upcoming updates.)
Creating a Route (early access)
A route is a planned path you build by tapping the map, then save with a name for later use. Route building works on both the convoy map and the planning map.
Open the map (convoy or planning).
Open "Work with Artifacts" and tap + ROUTE. The Route+ toolbar appears.
Tap New. A "Name this route" box appears with a suggested name — accept it or type your own — then start building.
Add is on by default (green): tap the map to drop points. If a trail or track is nearby, the point snaps to it and the magenta route line follows the trail's actual shape between your points — so the route traces real trails instead of cutting straight across. Tap away from any trail to place a free point exactly where you tapped. Tip: zoom in while building for the most reliable snapping.
Use Undo to remove the most recent point.
Pan and zoom freely between taps to position the map.
Tap Save to store the route. It is saved on your device, redraws on the map in magenta, and appears in Work with Artifacts → Routes under the name you gave it.
Tap Discard to leave without saving.
Coming next (not in this build):
Save In Progress / Resume: save a half-finished route and re-open it later to keep editing (the "In Progress" entry).
Draw and Suggest build methods (placeholders today).
Renaming/editing a saved route from the Routes list (route maintenance).
Route maintenance (rename, edit geometry, delete a completed route) lives in Work with Artifacts → Routes (SEL/Edit), not in the Route+ toolbar. The toolbar is for building only.
Track / Trail / Waypoint maintenance
Per-type maintenance (rename, detail, delete) is reached from each type's SEL/Edit list. trail/route/waypoint maintenance — in progress
Unnamed trails display as "Not Named." consistent labeling — being aligned at import
Manual maintenance note (internal): when a screen's functions change AND are complete, update that screen's section here and re-point its ? help anchor. Transitional radio-config sections (Section 3) are removed/rewritten in the 3.0 manual when those functions are replaced.

GroupTrack — User Manual (V2.5)
Cookbook style. Each section is one screen; every function on that screen is documented in place. The ? help icon on a screen deep-links to that screen's section here.
V2.5 · 2026-06-18 · Online edition: grouptrack.org/manual · Bundled offline copy ships in-app · Sections map 1:1 to the screens that carry a ? help icon.
How help links work: tapping ? on a screen opens this manual at that screen's section (the anchors below — #getting-started, #planning-map, #convoy-map, #artifacts, #radio-write). V2.5 scope for the ? icon: the screens that persist into 3.0 — Planning Map, Convoy Map (incl. the Meshtastic connection/monitoring panel), Work with Artifacts, and the Convoy radio-write menu. The goal in 3.0 is ? on every screen.
About the screen images: each chapter opens with an image of that landing screen — the screen you navigate from to reach its functions. Images show the landing screen, not every individual tap. (Image slots are marked below with their filenames; capture each screen and save it under the filename shown to drop it in.)
Contents
1. Getting Started — install, trails, map sources, radio

  1.2 Downloading trails

  1.4 Adding / updating trail sources

1 · Getting Started
First-time setup, in order. Do these once before your first ride; trail and tile data then persist on the device.
This chapter walks first-time setup from a fresh install through optional radio pairing. Each step persists: once you've imported trails and downloaded map tiles, they stay on the device across app updates and restarts — you don't redo this before every ride.
Draft note (remove before publish): the procedures in this chapter are drafted from current app behavior and prior notes. Steps marked [verify] need a confirming pass on the device to lock exact button labels / order before this ships to testers.
1.1 · Installing the software
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Install / first launchgs_install.png
Updating from an earlier version? Install as an update through the Play Store — do not uninstall the old version and clean-install, which breaks the installation. After updating, on first launch the trail/track database is rebuilt: re-import your trails (1.2), and your recorded tracks return automatically from your saved GPX files (open the track import screen and tap RESYNC TRACKS if any are missing).
Install GroupTrack from the Play Store internal-testing link the organizer sent you. [verify exact install path for testers]
Open the app. Grant the permissions it requests — location (for your position on the map) and storage/files (for trail data and map tiles). On first launch the app prepares its on-device databases.
If this is a fresh device (not an update), there is no trail data yet — continue to 1.2 to import trails for your area.
Requirements: Android 8.0+ (a tablet is recommended for map work). ~500 MB+ free for map tiles; trail data is roughly 15–30 MB per state. A radio (Meshtastic SenseCAP T1000-E or a LoRa device on firmware 2.6+) is only needed for convoy tracking, not for maps. Internet is needed once, to import trails and download tiles.
1.2 · Downloading trails
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Trail import (source / area)gs_download_trails.png
What you're doing: trail data is no longer bundled with the app. You import the trails for the regions where you ride, once, and they become permanent on your device.
Open the Planning Map.
Open Work with Artifacts and tap Import Trails. The trail source list appears.
Choose a method:
  Import by Source — select a land-management agency dataset (e.g. UGRC Utah Trails — ~49,000 trails + ~591 trailheads).
  Import by Area — draw a box on the map and see the sources that overlap it, with overlap percentages. processing fix in progress
On the validation screen, review the trail count and file size, then confirm to download. Trails and trailhead waypoints download as artifacts.
Fully close the app (force stop) and reopen so the new trail data loads.
If imported trails don't show: (1) fully close and reopen the app so trail data loads; (2) zoom in — trails draw at zoom level 8 and above, so a large dataset only appears when you're zoomed in enough. This is intentional for performance.
Full detail in Chapter 4 (Work with Artifacts).
1.3 · Adding / updating map sources
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Map sources / tile settingsgs_map_sources.png
What you're doing: map sources are the base imagery behind your trails (satellite, topo, outdoor, etc.). V2.5 offers 16 sources across 6 categories, and any source can be assigned to any of the three toolbar slots (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+).
Open Settings &gt; Map Sources. [verify menu path]
For each toolbar slot (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+), choose which of the 16 sources to assign.
For premium sources that require an API key (e.g. Thunderforest), enter the key when prompted; keys are stored locally on the device.
Changing a source triggers a background tile refresh for the new imagery.
Offline tiles: download tiles while you have internet so they're cached for offline use in the field. Tiles are served from your offline cache when available. See the Download Queue (Chapter 3) for managing tile downloads.
1.4 · Adding / updating trail sources
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Trail source cataloggs_trail_sources.png
What you're doing: beyond your first import (1.2), you can add more trail sources as you ride new areas, or update existing ones. Multiple sources and agencies can be active at once.
Open Work with Artifacts → Import Trails to return to the trail source catalog.
Add a source: pick another agency dataset (by source) or draw a new area (by area) and import, exactly as in 1.2.
Update a source: re-importing a source you already have is de-duplicated — trails already on the device are recognized and skipped, so re-import is safe and only adds what's new. [verify trail-source re-import dedupe state]
Agencies: UGRC Utah Trails is the first catalog source; BLM and USFS are planned.
1.5 · Setting up your radio (optional)
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Radio setup / pairinggs_radio_setup.png
What you're doing: the radio is only needed for live convoy tracking — maps, trails, and routes all work without it. If you're riding solo or just planning, you can skip this.
Power on your Meshtastic device (e.g. T1000-E).
Open the Convoy Map and open the connection panel (Chapter 3). Pair the device over Bluetooth; the panel shows connection state.
Apply the convoy radio configuration so all riders share the same channel and encryption — see Chapter 5 (Convoy Radio-Write Menu): Apply / Archive / Restore.
Confirm the mesh is up in the monitoring panel before relying on positions.
Device compatibility: some budget Android devices cannot hold a stable Bluetooth link to the radio (the connection drops after several seconds). If positions stop updating and the panel shows repeated disconnects, the device may be incompatible — see the tester compatibility list.

Save In Progress / Resume: save a half-finished route and re-open it later to keep editing (the "In Progress" entry).
Draw and Suggest build methods (placeholders today).
Renaming/editing a saved route from the Routes list (route maintenance).

Track / Trail / Waypoint maintenance

Screen: Convoy menu — radio configuration · ? help anchor: #radio-write
SCREEN IMAGE — Convoy Radio-Write menu (landing)radio_write.png

They are slated to be replaced in 3.0, but they work now and you should use them. This manual fully covers them; the 3.0 manual will rewrite this section when the functions change.
Apply Convoy Config (write to radio)
Connect the radio first (Chapter 3 connection panel) — the write action is unavailable with no Bluetooth link.
Open the Convoy menu → radio configuration.
Review the config values (channel, encryption keys, device settings). Values are validated before writing.
Apply. The write proceeds screen-by-screen / in passes through the config groups; confirm each completes.
Field validation: the config is validated (e.g. full field check) before programming. A two-pass programming approach is used so all config groups are written and confirmed.
Archive radio config
Save the current working radio configuration so it can be restored later. Use this before making changes.
Restore radio config
Re-apply a previously archived configuration to the connected radio.

GroupTrack — User Manual (V2.5)
Cookbook style. Each section is one screen; every function on that screen is documented in place. The ? help icon on a screen deep-links to that screen's section here.
V2.5 · 2026-06-18 · Online edition: grouptrack.org/manual · Bundled offline copy ships in-app · Sections map 1:1 to the screens that carry a ? help icon.
How help links work: tapping ? on a screen opens this manual at that screen's section (the anchors below — #getting-started, #planning-map, #convoy-map, #artifacts, #radio-write). V2.5 scope for the ? icon: the screens that persist into 3.0 — Planning Map, Convoy Map (incl. the Meshtastic connection/monitoring panel), Work with Artifacts, and the Convoy radio-write menu. The goal in 3.0 is ? on every screen.
About the screen images: each chapter opens with an image of that landing screen — the screen you navigate from to reach its functions. Images show the landing screen, not every individual tap. (Image slots are marked below with their filenames; capture each screen and save it under the filename shown to drop it in.)
Contents
1. Getting Started — install, trails, map sources, radio
  1.1 Installing the software
  1.2 Downloading trails
  1.3 Adding / updating map sources
  1.4 Adding / updating trail sources
  1.5 Setting up your radio (optional)
2. Planning Map — explore trails, build routes, import/manage artifacts off-radio
3. Convoy Map — live group tracking + Meshtastic connection &amp; monitoring panel
4. Work with Artifacts — trails, tracks, waypoints, routes (display, select/edit, create)
5. Convoy Radio-Write Menu — apply / archive / restore radio config transitional, supported in V2.5
1 · Getting Started
First-time setup, in order. Do these once before your first ride; trail and tile data then persist on the device.
This chapter walks first-time setup from a fresh install through optional radio pairing. Each step persists: once you've imported trails and downloaded map tiles, they stay on the device across app updates and restarts — you don't redo this before every ride.
Draft note (remove before publish): the procedures in this chapter are drafted from current app behavior and prior notes. Steps marked [verify] need a confirming pass on the device to lock exact button labels / order before this ships to testers.
1.1 · Installing the software
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Install / first launchgs_install.png
Updating from an earlier version? Install as an update through the Play Store — do not uninstall the old version and clean-install, which breaks the installation. After updating, on first launch the trail/track database is rebuilt: re-import your trails (1.2), and your recorded tracks return automatically from your saved GPX files (open the track import screen and tap RESYNC TRACKS if any are missing).
Install GroupTrack from the Play Store internal-testing link the organizer sent you. [verify exact install path for testers]
Open the app. Grant the permissions it requests — location (for your position on the map) and storage/files (for trail data and map tiles). On first launch the app prepares its on-device databases.
If this is a fresh device (not an update), there is no trail data yet — continue to 1.2 to import trails for your area.
Requirements: Android 8.0+ (a tablet is recommended for map work). ~500 MB+ free for map tiles; trail data is roughly 15–30 MB per state. A radio (Meshtastic SenseCAP T1000-E or a LoRa device on firmware 2.6+) is only needed for convoy tracking, not for maps. Internet is needed once, to import trails and download tiles.
1.2 · Downloading trails
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Trail import (source / area)gs_download_trails.png
What you're doing: trail data is no longer bundled with the app. You import the trails for the regions where you ride, once, and they become permanent on your device.
Open the Planning Map.
Open Work with Artifacts and tap Import Trails. The trail source list appears.
Choose a method:
  Import by Source — select a land-management agency dataset (e.g. UGRC Utah Trails — ~49,000 trails + ~591 trailheads).
  Import by Area — draw a box on the map and see the sources that overlap it, with overlap percentages. processing fix in progress
On the validation screen, review the trail count and file size, then confirm to download. Trails and trailhead waypoints download as artifacts.
Fully close the app (force stop) and reopen so the new trail data loads.
If imported trails don't show: (1) fully close and reopen the app so trail data loads; (2) zoom in — trails draw at zoom level 8 and above, so a large dataset only appears when you're zoomed in enough. This is intentional for performance.
Full detail in Chapter 4 (Work with Artifacts).
1.3 · Adding / updating map sources
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Map sources / tile settingsgs_map_sources.png
What you're doing: map sources are the base imagery behind your trails (satellite, topo, outdoor, etc.). V2.5 offers 16 sources across 6 categories, and any source can be assigned to any of the three toolbar slots (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+).
Open Settings &gt; Map Sources. [verify menu path]
For each toolbar slot (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+), choose which of the 16 sources to assign.
For premium sources that require an API key (e.g. Thunderforest), enter the key when prompted; keys are stored locally on the device.
Changing a source triggers a background tile refresh for the new imagery.
Offline tiles: download tiles while you have internet so they're cached for offline use in the field. Tiles are served from your offline cache when available. See the Download Queue (Chapter 3) for managing tile downloads.
1.4 · Adding / updating trail sources
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Trail source cataloggs_trail_sources.png
What you're doing: beyond your first import (1.2), you can add more trail sources as you ride new areas, or update existing ones. Multiple sources and agencies can be active at once.
Open Work with Artifacts → Import Trails to return to the trail source catalog.
Add a source: pick another agency dataset (by source) or draw a new area (by area) and import, exactly as in 1.2.
Update a source: re-importing a source you already have is de-duplicated — trails already on the device are recognized and skipped, so re-import is safe and only adds what's new. [verify trail-source re-import dedupe state]
Agencies: UGRC Utah Trails is the first catalog source; BLM and USFS are planned.
1.5 · Setting up your radio (optional)
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Radio setup / pairinggs_radio_setup.png
What you're doing: the radio is only needed for live convoy tracking — maps, trails, and routes all work without it. If you're riding solo or just planning, you can skip this.
Power on your Meshtastic device (e.g. T1000-E).
Open the Convoy Map and open the connection panel (Chapter 3). Pair the device over Bluetooth; the panel shows connection state.
Apply the convoy radio configuration so all riders share the same channel and encryption — see Chapter 5 (Convoy Radio-Write Menu): Apply / Archive / Restore.
Confirm the mesh is up in the monitoring panel before relying on positions.
Device compatibility: some budget Android devices cannot hold a stable Bluetooth link to the radio (the connection drops after several seconds). If positions stop updating and the panel shows repeated disconnects, the device may be incompatible — see the tester compatibility list.
2 · Planning Map
Screen: Planning Map · ? help anchor: #planning-map
SCREEN IMAGE — Planning Map (landing)planning_map.png
The Planning Map is the off-radio workspace: explore downloaded trails, import your track history, build and save routes, and manage what's displayed — all without a radio connected. It shares the spatial database and route engine with the Convoy Map, but keeps its own display state.
Map basics
Pan / zoom: drag to pan, pinch to zoom. These stay live at all times, even while building a route.
Base layers (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+): switch imagery from the layer control. Tiles are served from your offline cache when available. (Assign sources to these slots in Settings &gt; Map Sources — see 1.3.)
Viewport-aware display: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes load for the area you're viewing. Zoom in to see more detail; the display fills in as you move.
Displaying trails, tracks, waypoints, routes
See Chapter 4 (Work with Artifacts) — the toggle/select/edit controls are shared and documented there.
Too many trails in view: if the current view contains more trails than can be displayed at once, the SEL/Edit control indicates "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." Zoom in to narrow the area until trails become selectable. guidance behavior — coming
Building a route
See the full cookbook entry in Chapter 4 → Creating a Route. Route building works identically on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Importing trails / tracks
Import tracks (GPX): bring in your recorded track history. Large files import via streaming; duplicates (same geometry) are skipped automatically, and a recap shows new vs. already-in-library.
Import trails by area: draw an area to list and download trail sources overlapping it. processing fix in progress
Coming: waypoint and route extraction from GPX (all GPX imports are currently treated as tracks); GPX/KML open-with handler.
3 · Convoy Map
Screen: Convoy Map (incl. Meshtastic connection / monitoring panel) · ? help anchor: #convoy-map
SCREEN IMAGE — Convoy Map (landing)convoy_map.png
The Convoy Map is the live group-tracking screen used during a ride. It shows your position and the positions of other riders relayed over the Meshtastic LoRa mesh, plus the same trail/track/waypoint/route display and route-building tools as the Planning Map.
Connecting to your radio (connection &amp; monitoring panel)
Connect: open the connection panel and pair your Meshtastic device (e.g. T1000-E) over Bluetooth. The panel shows connection state.
Monitoring: the panel reports link status and node activity. Use it to confirm the mesh is up before relying on positions.
Device compatibility: some budget Android devices cannot hold a stable Bluetooth link to the radio (the connection drops after several seconds). If positions stop updating and the panel shows repeated disconnects, the device may be incompatible — see the tester compatibility list.
Live tracking
Rider positions: other riders appear as node markers, updated as mesh packets arrive.
Your position: driven by the phone GPS once location permission is granted.
Waypoints
Drop a waypoint: long-press the map to drop a waypoint pin.
Pin shape: waypoints display as teardrop pins — the pin's point marks the exact location you dropped it. Each waypoint type has its own color and icon.
Proximity: waypoints within 100 m are treated as the same location.
Help on this screen
? help: tap the ? button on the Convoy Map to open the release notes or the full user manual. (The same help is on the Planning Map; both open the same documents.)
Download QUEUES (tile downloads)
SCREEN IMAGE — Download Queues monitorqueues_download.png
QUEUES: opens the live download monitor (top-right) showing tile-download progress.
Manage the queue: hold (pause all processing, resume when ready), cancel a single entry, or cancel all. Downloaded tiles are preserved when you cancel a partial download.
Building a route on the Convoy Map
Identical to the Planning Map — see Chapter 4 → Creating a Route.
4 · Work with Artifacts
Screen: Work with Artifacts (shared by both maps)
SCREEN IMAGE — Work with Artifacts panel (landing)work_with_artifacts.png
"Work with Artifacts" is the control center for everything you display and create on the map: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes. The toggle and select/edit controls are the same on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Display toggles (ON / OFF / SELECTED)
ON: show all artifacts of that type in view.
OFF: hide that type.
SELECTED: show only the items you've checked in that type's select/edit list.
Select / Edit list (per type)
Open a type's SEL/Edit list to check individual items for SELECTED display, or to open an item's detail.
Search by name: choose an artifact type, type a name, and press Enter to find matching trails, tracks, waypoints, or routes by name across your whole database (not just what's on screen). Search is case-insensitive and matches partial names. Tap a result to open its detail.
Item detail: tapping an item's name (from a search result or the select/edit list) opens its detail card. The left side lists the actions available for that item's type; the right side shows the item's information. For trails this includes designated uses, surface type, classification (carto code), county, managing agency, and data source. Less-used technical values — bounding coordinates, created/updated dates, and the geometry hash — are tucked under a ▸ technical toggle so the useful information shows first; tap it to expand. Where a trail has alternate names on record, they appear here too. On the Convoy Map the detail is view-only; full editing is on the Planning Map.
FIT (fit to map): from an item's detail card, tap FIT to frame that item on the map. The map flies to the item and zooms to fit it, the item is selected and drawn on its own, and the other artifact types are turned off — so you see just the one you picked. Works for trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes, on both maps. FIT is how you go from finding a name to seeing it on the map.
List limit: the list currently shows up to 200 items. paging — coming
Trails over-limit: when more trails are in view than can be shown, SEL/Edit shows "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." coming
Track display
Tracks display as dashed green lines from your device's spatial database. When Tracks are on, each track shows direction-of-travel arrows along the line so you can read which way it runs — useful for telling a single looping track from two overlapping ones. The arrows are evenly spaced on screen and stay readable as you zoom, and are drawn in the same neon green as the track.
Routes display
Routes display as magenta lines, loaded from your device's spatial database the same viewport-aware way as trails and tracks. Build a route with + ROUTE (see Creating a Route). (Importing routes from GPX, and the Draw / Suggest build methods, are coming in upcoming updates.)
Creating a Route (early access)
A route is a planned path you build by tapping the map, then save with a name for later use. Route building works on both the convoy map and the planning map.
Open the map (convoy or planning).
Open "Work with Artifacts" and tap + ROUTE. The Route+ toolbar appears.
Tap New. A "Name this route" box appears with a suggested name — accept it or type your own — then start building.
Add is on by default (green): tap the map to drop points. If a trail or track is nearby, the point snaps to it and the magenta route line follows the trail's actual shape between your points — so the route traces real trails instead of cutting straight across. Tap away from any trail to place a free point exactly where you tapped. Tip: zoom in while building for the most reliable snapping.
Use Undo to remove the most recent point.
Pan and zoom freely between taps to position the map.
Tap Save to store the route. It is saved on your device, redraws on the map in magenta, and appears in Work with Artifacts → Routes under the name you gave it.
Tap Discard to leave without saving.

Save In Progress / Resume: save a half-finished route and re-open it later to keep editing (the "In Progress" entry).
Draw and Suggest build methods (placeholders today).
Renaming/editing a saved route from the Routes list (route maintenance).
Route maintenance (rename, edit geometry, delete a completed route) lives in Work with Artifacts → Routes (SEL/Edit), not in the Route+ toolbar. The toolbar is for building only.
