GroupTrack — Route Builder Blueprint
Method-1 (point-to-point snap-2) deliverable + scaffold for Methods 2/3 and drafts. Full flow, function targets, persistence model.
Captured 2026-06-03 from design session &nbsp;·&nbsp; TEMPORARY — fold into Living Checklist §E at recommit, then retire this file.
Status of this doc: scratch reference for the scaffolding pass. Everything here was decided in the 06-03 session and exists nowhere else yet. Once the scaffold is implemented and folded into the Living Checklist (§E Route Creation), delete this file.
A. The model in one paragraph
+ROUTE already exists on the Work-with-Artifacts panel (both maps). Tapping it collapses the artifacts panel and launches the Route+ toolbar in its place. The toolbar offers a single entry — "Start / Continue planning your route" — which opens a source picker (New / Continue in-progress / Copy completed). Three planning methods (point-to-point, draw, suggest) are toggles switchable mid-route, all feeding one shared vertex chain. The build loop is tap-to-place (snap-2) with Add/Undo. Editing is entirely in-memory until a deliberate Save. Exits are explicit and persistence-aware.
B. Snap-2 rule (Method 1, LIVE)
  Trail-first, strict. Within the radius, if ANY trail is in range, snap to the nearest point-on-line of a trail. Tracks are consulted ONLY when no trail is in range (a trail at 40m beats a track at 5m). Tracks fill gaps where no trail exists.
  Nearest-point-on-line, not nearest vertex. Radius is in meters (ground distance, haversine).
  No-snap = free-place. If neither trail nor track is in range, the point lands at the raw tapped coordinate. The segment to it is a straight line (crossing open ground / bridging a network gap). Final geometry, not a placeholder — no deferred snapping.
  Junction discipline. User drops a point AT each junction and selects the next trail explicitly. Between two consecutive snapped points on the SAME line, the segment is the trail-slice (sub-path of that line). Different line, or free point → straight segment. The route never auto-connects past a junction.
  WKT is LON-FIRST (LINESTRING(lon lat, ...)) — confirmed against SpatialDbManager.wktToGeoJsonCoords.
C. The three methods (toggle mid-route, shared chain)
  MethodGesturePan/zoomState
  1 · Point-to-point snap-2 LIVETap = place vertexPan + zoom livetapIntent=PLACE_VERTEX, dragIntent=PAN
  2 · Draw route SOONFinger-trace; snap-2 on each lift; line led ahead of finger (visual offset only — store true/snapped point)Pan OFF during trace, explicit toggle to repositiondragIntent=TRACE
  3 · Suggest routes SOONDrop key points → planner returns ~3-5 candidates w/ distance + POIsPan + zoom liveNeeds trail-network graph (topology) — far future; shapes .gpkg work
Two-axis rail: tapIntent (what a tap means) and dragIntent (PAN vs TRACE) are independent. A method is a named preset over the two. Build the dragIntent axis in from day one (pinned to PAN for Method 1) so Method 2 fills a branch instead of re-architecting the drag handler.
Methods combine per-segment. Finger-draw is specifically for paths VISIBLE on the tile but NOT in the spatial model. One route freely mixes tapped trail-slices, straight gap-bridges, and hand-traced segments — chosen per-segment, switched via the toolbar toggle.
D. Persistence model — in-memory until Save
  While working: in-memory only. The vertex chain lives in RouteManager.vertices. Zero file or DB impact during editing. The on-disk draft (if resumed) stays exactly as opened.
  In-progress drafts = private JSON in app-internal storage (context.filesDir, NOT the public Documents drive — not synced, not media-indexed, not user-visible as files). Carries the full vertex chain (lat/lon/lineId/lineType/segmentIndex/t/snapped) + name + last-modified. The chain preserves snap provenance so resume restores the builder exactly.
  Completed routes = spatial DB row (the routes table). Drafts NEVER touch the spatial DB. Only completed routes are eligible for AWS sync — this keeps the shared spatial model clean (no half-built routes propagate).
  A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row, never both. The transition is the one moment a delete pairs with an insert.
  Save = the only write (temp-then-rename for safety; create for NEW, overwrite for RESUMED). Discard = no write (drop memory, file untouched). Delete = remove file. No original-chain snapshot needed — disk is always the last-saved state.
E. Exit model (the part to get right)
Save completed (toolbar, always available, requires ≥2 vertices): buildWktAndBbox → insertRoute → delete draft file if one existed (graduation) → exit. This is the one affirmative "done" save.
Guarded exit — leaving with an un-completed route prompts, and the options depend on origin:
  OriginExit options
  NEW route (no file yet)Save as draft (create JSON) &nbsp;|&nbsp; Discard (no save, nothing was on disk)
  RESUMED draft (file exists)Save changes (overwrite JSON) &nbsp;|&nbsp; Discard changes (no save, file stays as opened) &nbsp;|&nbsp; Delete in-progress (remove file)
F. Work with Drafts
  List in-progress drafts (name + last-modified) — reads the private draft dir.
  Resume → load chain into memory → redraw partial route on current map → re-arm toolbar in add-point mode.
  Delete → remove draft file (nothing in DB to touch — no orphans).
G. Edit-of-existing
Completed routes are immutable (snap provenance is lost once flattened to LINESTRING). To change one: Copy a completed route as the starting chain for a NEW route (original untouched). Rename/delete of completed routes lives on the route maintenance screen (separate open item). True in-place re-edit deferred.
H. Deploy checklist — 13 user-contact points
  #ControlFunction targetFirst pass
  1+ROUTE (artifacts panel)onAddRoute → collapse panel + launch toolbarDEPLOY
  2Start / Continue planningopen source pickerDEPLOY
  3New routeclearRoute() → empty chainDEPLOY
  4Continue in-progressload draft JSON → repopulate + redrawSCAFFOLD
  5Copy a completed routefork completed → new chainSCAFFOLD
  6Method: Point-to-pointsnap + addVertex (live)DEPLOY
  7Method: Drawfinger-trace (dragIntent=TRACE)SCAFFOLD
  8Method: Suggestroute planner (graph)SCAFFOLD

First-pass working loop: deploy 1,2,3,6,9,10,12 → tap +ROUTE → New → place snapped points → Undo → Save completed → route saved + drawn. Everything else scaffolded as a visible "coming soon" placeholder linked to its checklist item. Discard exit works trivially (drop memory). Draft Save + RESUMED path activate with the draft-I/O patch.
I. Logic already built (in RouteManager, undeployed)
  SnapResult, parseWktLine (lon-first), haversineMeters, nearestOnSegment, nearestPointOnLines, snap (trail-first/track-fallback).
  Vertex, builder state (addVertex/undoVertex/clearRoute/routeVertices), sliceLine (direction-correct), buildSegments, buildWktAndBbox.
  DB side exists: insertRoute, queryRoutesByViewport; route JS bridge updateRoutes/showRoutes wired (gold dashed). Nav route ConvoyRoutes.ConvoyRouteCreate wired to a stub screen.
J. Scaffold build order
  +ROUTE → collapse artifacts panel + launch Route+ toolbar — BOTH screens, identical, one pass (avoid drift).
  Bridge: onMapTap mirroring onMapLongPress, gated on route mode — both screens.
  JS: route-mode polyline draw (feed building chain via existing route path) — both map HTMLs.
  Toolbar UI: method toggles + Add/Undo + Save-completed + guarded Exit; placeholders for Draw/Suggest/drafts.
  Deferred (separate patch): draft file I/O — Save/Resume/Delete in private storage; activates checklist items 4,5,11,13.

  var d=document.getElementById('demo');

  function drawDemo(id){

Route+ Toolbar — UI PACT
The agreed UI spec for route creation. Build the actual Route+ toolbar against this. Approved look &amp; feel: RouteBuilder_Toolbar_FINAL_v3.
Locked 2026-06-04 &nbsp;·&nbsp; supersedes the look-and-feel mockups &nbsp;·&nbsp; the build target for the snap-2 slice
The test this pact enforces: when the panel is built, every use case with a defined action must appear on the panel (or be explicitly assigned to Work-with-Artifacts → Routes) with its proper action associated. No orphan actions; no actions without a home.
1. Panel split rule
The Route+ toolbar is for CREATE / BUILD only. Every other route action — copy a completed route, edit / rename / delete a completed route, view detail — lives in the Work-with-Artifacts panel under Routes (SEL/EDIT). Toolbar = build; artifacts panel = manage.
2. Panel behavior (real-estate)
  BehaviorHowNote
  Accordion collapse / expandchevron on header; collapses to header (Route+ + point count)same pattern as Work-with-Artifacts panel
  Draggablededicated grip handle (top strip)drag on the handle ONLY — never on a tap control (avoids the QUEUES tap-vs-drag collision)
  Save / Discard always visiblesingle-level toolbar row; stays reachable even when the build controls are collapsedfrequently-used exit actions — never hidden behind the accordion
  Position + state persistenceremember last position + collapsed state, per mapties to the session map-JSON idea (TBD when built)
3. Control inventory — toolbar (build only)
  GroupControlStateAction
  Start / continueNewLIVEclearRoute() → empty chain, Add ON
  Amend In-Progress Routessoonlist in-progress draft routes → resume one → load draft JSON → repopulate + redraw
  MethodPoint-tapLIVEtap = place snapped vertex (snap-2, trail-first / track-fallback)
  Drawsoonfinger-trace (dragIntent = TRACE)
  Suggestsoondrop key points → planner returns candidates
  BuildAdd (state toggle)LIVEGREEN on entry = taps place points; press → RED = taps pan/reposition. ON on entry unless another method is chosen. Status echoed on a map chip.
  UndoLIVEundoVertex() → redraw
  Exit (adaptive, always visible)SaveLIVE*Adaptive. New, ≥2 pts → Save as completed (buildWktAndBbox → insertRoute + delete draft if any). New → Save in-progress (create draft JSON). Resumed → Save as completed | Save with changes (overwrite draft). *completed-save LIVE; in-progress draft save = soon.
  DiscardLIVE*Adaptive. New (no draft) → clear from screen, no write. Resumed → prompt: Roll back to original (no write) | Delete entire in-progress (remove draft JSON). *clear-new LIVE; resumed legs = soon.
4. Lives elsewhere — Work-with-Artifacts → Routes (SEL/EDIT)
  ActionNote
  Copy a completed routefork completed → new chain. NOT on the toolbar (was redundant — removed).
  Edit / rename / delete completed routeroute maintenance via the SEL/EDIT list
  Route detaildetail from the list row (not map-tap — thin lines are poor touch targets)
5. The only write points (persistence model)
Everything is in-memory while building. The ONLY writes: Save in-progress (create draft JSON), Save with changes (overwrite draft JSON), Save as completed (insertRoute DB row + delete draft JSON if one existed — graduation). NEVER written on: Roll back, Discard, remove-unsaved. A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row, never both. Drafts = private JSON in app-internal storage; completed = spatial DB row.
6. First-pass working loop (the snap-2 slice we build next)
+ROUTE → New (Add ON) → place snapped points → toggle Add OFF / collapse / drag aside to see the map → Undo as needed → Save as completed → buildWktAndBbox → insertRoute → route saved as DB row, drawn gold dashed → exit. Discard (new route) clears the screen, no write. Everything marked "soon" is a visible placeholder linked to its checklist item; the draft-JSON legs (Amend In-Progress, in-progress Save, roll-back) activate with the draft-I/O pass.
7. Logic already built (RouteManager, undeployed)
SnapResult, parseWktLine (lon-first), haversineMeters, nearestOnSegment, nearestPointOnLines, snap (trail-first/track-fallback), Vertex, addVertex/undoVertex/clearRoute/routeVertices, sliceLine, buildSegments, buildWktAndBbox. DB: insertRoute, queryRoutesByViewport; JS bridge updateRoutes/showRoutes wired (gold dashed). Nav route ConvoyRoutes.ConvoyRouteCreate wired to a stub screen. The snap-2 slice wires the toolbar to this existing logic.

      RIDES RULES
      CREATE RIDE only accessible if is_organizer = TRUE and organizer_terms_accepted_at is set.
      Private rides: invite link only. No broadcast. No discovery. No email.
      Public rides: broadcast to followers via email. Discoverable in Explore. No personal invite link.
      broadcast_sent flag is permanent once set. API returns 409 if broadcast attempted twice. Button disabled.
      Invite acceptance triggers: ride download + map tile download + enrollment POST. All automatic.
      Map tiles download uses bounds from rides.map_bounds_* set by organizer at ride creation.

      TRACKS RULES
      Difficulty score numeric: Easy = 1.0, Moderate = 2.0, Hard = 3.0. Average computed from all survey responses for rides that used this track.
      Would ride again % = COUNT(recommend=Yes) / COUNT(*) from ride_surveys for rides using this track.
      Downloading a track automatically queues map tile download for the track bounding box. Same mechanism as invite acceptance.
      Track detail is an inline expand panel — not a separate screen. Tap to expand, shows mini map with GPX line, distance, elevation, stats, would ride again %, download button.
      USE AS ROUTE sets rides.route_id when organizer creates next ride. Track selected from library, not imported again.
      SOLO mode riders can download tracks as reference overlays on the map. No radio or ride needed.
      SCHEMA ADDITIONS — TRACKS
      ride_tracks.bounds_north DECIMAL(10,7) NULL — computed at upload
      ride_tracks.bounds_south DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
      ride_tracks.bounds_east DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
      ride_tracks.bounds_west DECIMAL(10,7) NULL

          Simple Track Save
          No survey. Track name required — SAVE disabled until filled. Track saved to device tracks directory. No database impact. No donation.
            Track name
            Saved to filesDir/my_tracks/
            GPX format (default)
        → Map (IDLE)
        DIALOG BORGANIZED
          Survey + Track Save
          Three checkboxes above track name. Fast — 15 seconds in field. Survey queued locally, uploads when connectivity returns. Track donated if share checked.
            Difficulty: Easy/Moderate/Hard
            Would ride again: Yes/No
            Share track with community: Yes/No
            Track name (pre-filled from ride name)
            SKIP SURVEY saves track only
            ride_surveys queued locally
            ride_tracks uploaded if shared
        → Map (IDLE)
      STOP RECORD RULES
      RideState determines which dialog appears. SOLO or CONVOY → Dialog A. ORGANIZED → Dialog B.
      Track name pre-populated from active ride name in ORGANIZED state. Rider can edit.
      SAVE disabled until track name is not empty in both dialogs.
      Survey queued to SharedPreferences immediately. Uploaded via PATCH /ride/survey on next connectivity — radio offline is irrelevant.
      Track donation: MD5 computed on device, POST /ride/survey with track_donation payload. Silent discard if hash exists.
      Post-ride notes entered later from Ride History expand panel — not at STOP time. No notes field in the field dialog.
    🗄
      SCHEMA CHANGES REQUIRED
      All additions to RDS identified tonight — apply before Phase B
      ALTER TABLE statements only — no existing columns modified
    12 COLUMNS
    ▼
        rides TABLE
        start_time TIME NULL
        trailhead_lat DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
        trailhead_lon DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
        trailhead_name VARCHAR(255) NULL
        latitude DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
        longitude DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
        users TABLE
        default_radius_miles TINYINT DEFAULT 50
        latitude DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
        longitude DECIMAL(10,7) NULL

        fcm_token_updated DATETIME NULL
        ride_tracks TABLE
        bounds_north DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
        bounds_south DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
        bounds_east DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
        bounds_west DECIMAL(10,7) NULL
        DEPLOYMENT NOTE
        All nullable — no existing rows affected

        No data migration needed
        FCM columns added when Firebase integrated (V3.1)

      RIDESTATE RULES
      Three states controlling map display, survey, and track donation
      Computed every tick · Channel name + date match · Zero V2.4 behavior change
    3 STATES
    ▼
        SOLO
        Node count ≤ 1, no ride loaded
          🗺 GPS trail in real time
          ⏹ Simple save dialog
          📤 No donation
          🗄 No DB impact
        CONVOY

function toggle(id) {
  const el = document.getElementById(id);
  el.classList.toggle('open');
}
function toggleAll() {
  const sections = document.querySelectorAll('.section');
  const allOpen = Array.from(sections).every(s => s.classList.contains('open'));
  sections.forEach(s => allOpen ? s.classList.remove('open') : s.classList.add('open'));
  document.querySelector('.expand-all').textContent = allOpen ? 'EXPAND ALL' : 'COLLAPSE ALL';
}
function scrollTo(id) {
  document.getElementById(id).scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth', block:'start'});
  if (!document.getElementById(id).classList.contains('open')) toggle(id);
}

GroupTrack V2.5 — User Manual
Screen-by-screen cookbook · Off-road convoy tracking &amp; trail navigation · grouptrack.org
How this manual works. This is a cookbook, not a reference list — it follows what you actually do. Each screen lists where it’s reached from, what you do there, and what it leads to. This edition covers the V2.5 heart of the app: the two maps and everything that feeds them (trails, tracks, routes, waypoints, downloads) plus organizer radio setup. Account, dashboard, and ride-management screens are part of the Release 3.0 cloud rewrite and are not documented here. Screenshots are added per screen in a following revision (live device capture).
Contents
1. Maps, Trails &amp; Tracks (the heart of V2.5)
2. Offline Maps &amp; Downloads
3. Radio Setup (Organizer)
Appendix — V2.5 Feature Status
1. Maps, Trails &amp; Tracks (the heart of V2.5)
The two maps and everything that feeds them. This is where V2.5’s big changes live — icon-driven Work with Artifacts, universal search, the unified artifact detail panel, and trail import.
The right-edge icon column — how you reach everything on a map.Both maps share a vertical icon column on the right edge: a search icon (magnifying glass), a Work with Artifacts icon, and a ? help icon. Tapping the Work with Artifacts icon opens that panel expanded; collapsing the accordion closes it. The old always-on Work-with-Artifacts bar is gone — it’s an icon now. On the Planning (Map Viewer) map the panel has full editing and import; on the Convoy (live) map the same panel is display-only (no editing or import during live convoy operations).
Convoy (Live Map)
Reached from: Dashboard / active ride
The live ride view — your group’s vehicles in real time. The right-edge icon column gives you search, Work with Artifacts (display-only here: toggle Trails / Tracks / Waypoints / Routes), and help. Header shows the tile source, QUEUES, and the zoom readout (N · Z##). Track direction is shown with pixel-spaced neon arrows along each track.
Leads to: Map Viewer · Track Export · Track Import · Settings
[ screenshot to be added ]
Map Viewer (Planning Map)
Reached from: Convoy map / active ride planning
Plan a ride: search, download tiles, and manage artifacts. Work with Artifacts here has full import + edit. Use the search icon to find any artifact; use Work with Artifacts → IMPORT TRAILS to open Trail Sources. QUEUES manages downloads. The map remembers your last viewport and selection between visits.
Leads to: Trail Sources (IMPORT TRAILS) · Track Import · Track Export
[ screenshot to be added ]
Universal search (both maps)
The search icon opens a single search across five modes — Area · Track · Route · Trail · Waypoint. Pick a mode, search, and tap a result to open the unified artifact detail panel for it. This one search replaces the older per-map, per-type search entry points.
The artifact detail panel + Carto Type
One detail panel serves every artifact, reached three ways: from a search result, from a SELECT/Edit list row, or by tapping an artifact on the map. It shows the artifact’s rider-facing details with a collapsible technical section, plus action buttons (rename, change type, delete, share/export, and FIT — recenter the map to the artifact). For trails it shows a Carto Type band — the trail’s classification (OHV / Road-Concurrent, Hiking &amp; Biking, Hiking-Only, Paved Shared Use, and so on, or “Unspecified”), colored by its carto color. The same carto type now also appears in the map popup when you tap a trail line.
Artifact types
TrailsToggle ON to display trail overlays from the spatial database, loaded dynamically for your current viewport. Trail lines draw in cyan; the trail’s classification color shows in its detail-panel Carto Type band and in the map popup. Trails display at zoom 8+; zoom in to see them.
TracksToggle ON to display your recorded GPS tracks from the spatial database, loaded by viewport like trails. Tracks appear as neon green (#39FF14) dashed lines, with pixel-spaced direction arrows. Tapping a track shows its name (from the GPX filename).
WaypointsToggle to display user-created waypoints. 10+ standard types: trailhead, fuel, gate, hazard, scenic viewpoint, water source, camp, parking, junction, rally, and others. Drop one by long-pressing the map on empty ground (not on a vehicle marker) — a type picker opens.
RoutesToggle to display saved routes from the spatial database, the same viewport-aware way as trails and tracks. Build a route with “+ ROUTE” (see “Creating a Route”). Routes display as magenta lines.
The CartoCode color legend
A trail’s classification is encoded as a CartoCode (the leading digit of its type label). The colors:
1 — Hiking-Only (yellow)
2 — Hiking &amp; Biking Allowed (orange)
3 — Paved Shared Use (teal)
4 — OHV / Road-Concurrent (blue)
5 — Biking-Only (purple)
6 — Equestrian (brown)
7 — Steps (grey)
8 — Bridge / Tunnel (rose)
default / unclassified (cyan)
Trail lines on the map draw cyan by design; the classification color appears in the artifact detail panel’s Carto Type band and in the trail’s map popup.
SELECT / Edit and the three-state controlSELECT/Edit opens the artifact list for a type, scoped to the current view: a checkbox per item, Select All / Deselect All, and per-item actions. Each type also has a three-state display control — ON (show all in view), OFF (hide), and SELECTED (show only the items you checked). Each map remembers its own display selections independently: what you pick on the Convoy map no longer carries over to the Planning map.
FIT — recenter to an artifactFIT (in the artifact detail panel) recenters and zooms the map to frame the selected artifact with a small margin, and keeps it selected. Use it to jump straight to a trail, track, route, or waypoint you’ve found in search or the list.
Creating a Route (early access)
Open the map (Convoy or Planning) and open Work with Artifacts, then tap “+ ROUTE”. The Route+ toolbar appears.
Tap “New”. A “Name this route” box appears with a suggested name — accept it or type your own — then tap “Start”.
Tap “Add” (it turns green), then tap the map to drop each point. Each point snaps to the nearest trail or track if one is close by, so your route follows established paths; tap away from any trail to place a free point exactly where you tapped. A magenta line connects your points in order.
Use “Undo” to remove the most recent point. Pan and zoom freely between taps to reposition the map.
Tap “Save” to store the route. It is saved on your device, redraws on the map in magenta, and appears in Work with Artifacts → Routes under the name you gave it. Tap “Discard” to leave without saving.
To move the Route+ toolbar around the map, the panel must be expanded (accordion open). Drag the grip handle in the header to reposition; when collapsed, tapping the header expands it rather than moving it.
Routes display in magenta. Saved routes load from the spatial database the same viewport-aware way as trails and tracks. Saving a half-finished route to resume later (“In Progress”), editing a saved route’s geometry, and the Draw and Suggest methods are coming in upcoming updates.
Import Artifacts &amp; RESYNC TRACKS
Open Work with Artifacts and choose Import; pick your GPX file (the picker opens your device storage). Large files are processed one track at a time, so even big exports import without crashing.
When it finishes, a recap shows “X new / Y already in library.” New tracks draw on the map immediately. (If the artifact list looks empty, leave the screen and return — known refresh gap; the data is saved.)
Duplicates are identified by shape (geometry), not name: re-importing the same file is safe and shows “0 new / N already in library.”
RESYNC TRACKS recovers device track files that aren’t in the database (e.g. after an update): it scans my_tracks/ and adds any track not already saved. Run it again to confirm — a second run should add 0.
Tracks only, this build: importing a GPX brings in its tracks; waypoints and routes inside the file are skipped for now (separate import coming). The list caps at 200 shown — larger libraries are paged in a later build.
Trail &amp; track displayWhen you open the Planning Map, GroupTrack scans your my_tracks/ directory and syncs any new GPX files into the spatial database in the background (it doesn’t block the map). Files already in the database are skipped. As you pan and zoom, the track query updates automatically (400 ms debounce) so only visible tracks load — instant response even with large libraries.The current release includes trail data for the Utah / northern-Arizona corridor. Additional regional datasets will be downloadable in future updates through the Trail Source Manager. Trails load by viewport using bounding-box indexing; below zoom 8 they are hidden for readability.
Trail Sources
Reached from: Map Viewer → Work with Artifacts → IMPORT TRAILS
Browse approved trail sources and import them. The screen opens on Select Source — pick a source (e.g. UGRC Utah Trails), VALIDATE, then IMPORT TRAILS to download its trails (and any trailhead waypoints). A live recap counts records as they process (processed · new · dupes · aliased · already-imported). Already-imported sources show a green check but remain selectable — re-select one and run it again to reprocess it (refreshes trail classification / carto data on the existing trails without changing geometry). A separate By Area method imports the sources overlapping an area you draw on the map. After importing, close &amp; reopen the app, then zoom in to see the trails.
Leads to: Back to Map Viewer with trails imported / updated
[ screenshot to be added ]
Map Sources
Reached from: Settings → Map Sources
Assign any of 16 tile sources (Google, Esri, USGS, OpenTopo, OSM, Thunderforest, CartoDB) to your SAT / TOPO / TOPO+ buttons. Add custom sources by URL; manage API keys per source.
Leads to: Back to Settings
[ screenshot to be added ]
Route Create
Reached from: Map Viewer (route planning)
Create a route with the point-to-point, snap-to-trail/track method (see “Creating a Route”). Freehand draw and source-suggest methods are deferred.
Leads to: Back to Map Viewer with route saved
[ screenshot to be added ]
Track Import
Reached from: Convoy / Map Viewer → Track Import
Import tracks from Downloads (GPX/KML). RESYNC TRACKS rebuilds from my_tracks/. A recap dialog reports new / already-in-library counts.
Leads to: Back to map
[ screenshot to be added ]
Tracks / Track Export
Reached from: Convoy → Track Export
View and export your tracks (GPX). Export to Downloads or email.
Leads to: Back to map
[ screenshot to be added ]
2. Offline Maps &amp; Downloads
Pull map tiles for offline use and manage the download queue.
Download queue. The QUEUES button on both maps opens the queue management panel showing active, queued, and completed downloads. Controls: Hold (pause processing), Resume, Cancel Entry (remove one), and Cancel All (stop and clear). Transfer concurrency is settable (default 4, max 6). The controls are functional in the backend; the live-data queue panel UI is being wired in the next update.
Download Ride Config
Reached from: Ride config / invite acceptance
Download the map area + config for a ride you’re joining.
Leads to: Map with tiles + config applied

function filterDoc(q){
  q=q.trim().toLowerCase();
  var blocks=document.querySelectorAll('main .screen, main .box, main h1, main h2, main .coming, main .intro, main .toc, main .row, main .legend');
  if(!q){blocks.forEach(b=>b.classList.remove('hidden'));return;}
  blocks.forEach(function(b){
    if(b.classList.contains('toc')){b.classList.add('hidden');return;}
    b.classList.toggle('hidden', b.textContent.toLowerCase().indexOf(q)===-1);
  });
}

GroupTrack V2.5 — Release Notes
What's new · Field Test Release · Updated 2026-06-21 · grouptrack.org
  ⚠ Updating from an earlier version? Read this first.
  Install as an UPDATE — do NOT uninstall the old version and install this as a new install.
  Let the app update in place through the Play Store. Uninstalling and then clean-installing
  will break the installation, and you will have to reach out for help to recover it.
  After the update, on first launch the trail/track database is rebuilt. So:
    Re-import your trails — open Work with Artifacts → Import Trails and import UGRC Utah Trails again (brings back trails + trailhead waypoints).
    Your recorded tracks come back automatically from your saved GPX files on launch. If any track is missing, open the track import screen and tap RESYNC TRACKS.
    Your GPX track files and downloaded map tiles are not affected by the update.
  If you already did a clean install and it’s broken: the fix is to remove the two GroupTrack database files from /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/ before relaunching — contact the organizer for help, as this is a manual step.
What's new in this build
  Find anything, then fit it to your screen
  One search on either map covers Areas, Tracks, Routes, Trails, and Waypoints. Tap a result to open its detail, then tap FIT to fly the map to it and frame it on its own.
  Benefit: jump straight to the trail or track you mean, instead of hunting the map.
  Manual: Universal search · the detail panel · FIT
  One detail panel for every artifact
  Trails, tracks, routes, and waypoints all open the same detail panel — from a search result, a select/edit row, or by tapping the artifact on the map. Rename, change type, share, or delete from one place.
  Benefit: the same simple panel everywhere, so you always know where the controls are.
  Manual: The artifact detail panel
  Trail type and color, on the trail itself
  Each trail’s classification — OHV / Road-Concurrent, Hiking &amp; Biking, Hiking-Only, Paved Shared Use, and so on — shows as a colored Carto Type band in its detail panel, and now also in the popup when you tap a trail on the map.
  Benefit: tell at a glance which trails are open to your vehicle.
  Manual: Carto Type · the CartoCode color legend
  Refresh trail data without starting over
  In Trail Sources, an already-imported source now stays selectable. Pick it again and run it to refresh trail classification and details on the trails you already have — your geometry and recorded tracks are untouched. A live recap counts records as they process.
  Benefit: pull updated trail info anytime, without re-downloading from scratch.
  Manual: Trail Sources
  Help on both maps
  The ? button that opens the manual and release notes is on the Convoy Map as well as the Planning Map.
  Benefit: help is one tap away wherever you are.
  Manual: Convoy &amp; Planning maps
  Clearer direction arrows on tracks
  Direction-of-travel arrows on tracks are evenly spaced on screen and stay readable as you zoom, drawn in the same neon green as the track.
  Benefit: read which way a track runs at a glance, even on long tracks.
  Manual: Tracks
  Each map remembers where you left it
  The Convoy and Planning maps each restore their own last view and what you had selected, independently of each other.
  Benefit: pick up exactly where you were, on the right map.
  Manual: Maps
  Build routes that follow real trails
  Tap to drop points and each one snaps to the nearest trail or track; tap away from a trail to place a free point. Name it and save (early access).
  Benefit: lay out a route along established paths in seconds.
  Manual: Creating a Route
Also in V2.5
  Bring your own trail data
  Trail data is no longer bundled with the app. You import the regions where you ride — by Source (pick a land agency) or by Area (draw a box). One-time, a few minutes on WiFi; it’s permanent on your device after that.
  Benefit: trails for the places you actually ride, across many states and agencies.
  Manual: Trail Sources
  Faster maps with the spatial database
  Trails and tracks load only for the part of the map you’re looking at, from an on-device spatial database. Tracks sync in automatically from your GPX files on launch.
  Benefit: instant pan and zoom even with tens of thousands of trails.
  Manual: Trail &amp; track display
  Work with Artifacts, now icon-driven
  A right-edge icon column on both maps gives you search, Work with Artifacts, and help. The panel opens expanded and collapses closed — the old always-on bar is gone.
  Benefit: more map, controls one tap away when you want them.
  Manual: The right-edge icon column
  More map sources, and download controls
  16 tile sources (Google, Esri, USGS, OpenTopo, OSM, Thunderforest, CartoDB) assignable to your SAT / TOPO / TOPO+ buttons, with API-key management. The download queue supports hold, resume, cancel, and a settable number of simultaneous downloads.
  Benefit: the basemaps you prefer, and control over big offline downloads.
  Manual: Map Sources · Offline Maps &amp; Downloads
Open the full User Manual &#8594;

  V3.0 MAP FUNCTIONS DEFINITION · APRIL 10, 2026 · CONFIDENTIAL
    01 Map Architecture
      V3.0 separates map functionality into two distinct maps. The Convoy Map remains operational and focused. The Planning Map is a new greenfield screen in the Maps section of the bottom nav.
          MapPurposeFunctions
              CONVOY MAP
              Operational — launched from main nav during a ride
              Live node tracking, HUD, track recording, layer switch, NET/LOCAL toggle, show downloaded areas, KML/GPX overlay (read-only, from library)
              PLANNING MAP
              Planning — dedicated Maps section in bottom nav
              Waypoint creation, track/route overlays, area search, tile download management, layer preferences, storage management, AWS coverage display, route planner, download region draw
      Rule: Planning Map functions never bleed into Convoy Map. During a ride the screen stays clean and operationally focused. All asset management lives in the Maps section.
      Map Bar — Two-Row Layout (V2.4 Current)
          T
          TRAILHEAD
            ▼
            MAP &nbsp;SAT
              NET
            SAT
            HYB
            TOPO
            RD
        CURRENT VIEWPORT — ASSETS SHOWN WITHIN THIS AREA ONLY
    02 Asset Types
        ⬛ TRACK
        Recorded path — already ridden. GPX or KML. Solid line display. Color from assigned palette or default #6B4EFF.
        -- ROUTE
        Planned path — not yet ridden. GPX or KML. Dashed line display. Orange #F5A623. Types: LOOP, OUT &amp; BACK, POINT TO POINT.
        ⊙ TRAILHEAD
        Named meeting/start point. Waypoint subtype with icon_type=TRAILHEAD. Always visible on map regardless of toggle state.
        ⬡ WAYPOINT
        Single named point. Types: HAZARD, LANDMARK, MEETING POINT. Standard pins, OFF by default in layer panel.
    03 Track Storage Rules
        FolderContents
          mytracks/recorded/GPS recordings from GroupTrack
          mytracks/imported/Files brought in via file picker from Downloads
          mytracks/rides/{ride_id}/Auto-created when track associated with a ride. Copy of track — original in imported/ remains.
    Hard rule: All tracks stored in mytracks/ folder or subfolders — no exceptions. File picker scans Downloads only, GPX and KML files only. Import copies file — original remains in Downloads.
    04 Vignette Display Rules
    A vignette is a small map thumbnail shown on any card that references spatial data. Used consistently everywhere — import list, ride cards, track library, dashboard invite cards, route list. Tile source: HYB tiles (satellite + labels gives best context).
        PriorityConditionDisplay
          1Track existsTrack line (solid, 2.5px, purple #6B4EFF) over HYB tile background
          2Route existsRoute line (dashed, 2px, orange #F5A623) over HYB tile background
          3Trailhead onlyOrange pin marker centered on trailhead location
          4Bounding box onlyArea rectangle with no line
          5No spatial dataGeneric map grid placeholder
        ContextHeight
          Import list card / Ride card (Dashboard, My Rides)Full card width × 80px
          Track Detail / Route DetailFull card width × 165px
          Ride DetailFull card width × 120px
    05 Layer Panel — Accordion Display
        Accordion pattern — one section open at a time. Type-level toggles only — no individual asset visibility control. No preferences stored — always opens with all types ON, all sections collapsed.
            ToggleDefaultControls
              ⊙ TRAILHEADSONAll trailhead pins in viewport
              ⬛ TRACKSONAll recorded tracks in viewport
              -- ROUTESONAll planned routes in viewport
              ↯ GPX / KMLONAll imported files in viewport
              ⬡ WAYPOINTSOFFAll standard waypoints in viewport
        LAYERS
            ⊙
            TRAILHEADS
            (3)
            ▶
            TRACKS
            (12)
            ▼
            ROUTES
            (4)
              Gooseberry Mesa Loop
              14.2 mi · MODERATE · LOOP
              Hurricane Cliffs
              22.1 mi · HARD · OUT &amp; BACK
            ▶
            GPX / KML
            (2)
            ▶
            WAYPOINTS
            (8 hidden)
    06 Viewport-Driven Display
    Hard rule: Only assets whose geometry intersects the current map viewport are shown — no exceptions. List and map display are always in sync. No asset appears in the list that is not visible in the current viewport.
        Zoom LevelDisplay Rule
          Below z10No assets rendered — layer panel shows "Zoom in to see assets"
          z10 – z13Trailheads only, clustered
          z14 – z16Trailheads + track/route lines simplified, waypoints clustered
          z17 – z18Full detail, all types, all points, labels visible
    07 Layer Z-Order
        1
        Tile base layer (SAT / HYB / TOPO / RD)
        2
        Downloaded area overlay (blue fill)
        3
        AWS available overlay (second color — V3 addition)
        4
        Tracks (solid lines, oldest to newest)
        5
        Routes (dashed lines)
        6
        Waypoints (standard pins)
        7
        Trailheads (always visible, above standard waypoints)
        8
        Active ride route (always on top of asset layers)
        9
        UI overlays (node markers, HUD)
    08 Bounding Box Auto-Calculation
        SourceRule
          Track attached to rideMin bounding box of all track points + 1 mile buffer on each edge
          Route attached to rideMin bounding box of all route points + 1 mile buffer on each edge
          Trailhead only (no track/route)Manual draw — map flies to trailhead, organizer draws rectangle
          No spatial dataManual draw only — same as V2.4 download flow
    Rule: 1 mile buffer on each edge is the recommended default. Organizer can adjust the suggested bounding box before confirming download. Buffer measured from outermost track/route points.
    09 Ride Creation — Hard Gate
    A ride CANNOT be saved without a map boundary. SAVE button is disabled and shows "MAP AREA REQUIRED" until a bounding area exists.
        PrioritySourceResult
          1Attach a trackBounding box auto-calculated from track points + 1 mile buffer
          2Attach a routeBounding box auto-calculated from route points + 1 mile buffer
          3Draw manuallyDraw tool activated — organizer draws rectangle on Planning Map
    10 Download Layer Preferences
    User selects which layers to download. No preferences are mandated — user decides. Default recommendation: HYB only.
        LayerDefaultStorage (relative)Notes
          SATOFFBaseline (1×)Satellite imagery only — no labels
          HYBON~1× (same as SAT)Recommended — satellite + trail/road labels
          TOPOOFF~0.6×Terrain contours — useful for elevation planning
          RDOFF~0.3×Lightest layer — road/POI only
    SAT + HYB together = ~2× storage for same satellite imagery. Users who want both should understand the duplication. At least one layer must remain checked.
    11 RDS Schema
-- tracks
track_id, user_id, ride_id (nullable), name,
difficulty ENUM('EASY','MODERATE','HARD'),
distance_mi FLOAT, file_path VARCHAR(500),
bounds_n DOUBLE, bounds_s DOUBLE, bounds_e DOUBLE, bounds_w DOUBLE,
trailhead_lat DOUBLE, trailhead_lon DOUBLE, created_at
-- routes
route_id, user_id, name,
type ENUM('LOOP','OUT_AND_BACK','POINT_TO_POINT'),
difficulty ENUM('EASY','MODERATE','HARD'),
distance_mi FLOAT, file_path VARCHAR(500),
bounds_n DOUBLE, bounds_s DOUBLE, bounds_e DOUBLE, bounds_w DOUBLE,
trailhead_lat DOUBLE, trailhead_lon DOUBLE, created_at
-- waypoints (includes trailheads via icon_type)
waypoint_id, user_id, ride_id (nullable), name, description,
icon_type ENUM('TRAILHEAD','HAZARD','LANDMARK','MEETING_POINT'),
lat DOUBLE, lon DOUBLE,
parking_available BOOLEAN, facilities TEXT, access_notes TEXT,
created_at
-- rides (additions)
trailhead_lat DOUBLE, trailhead_lon DOUBLE,
route_id INT REFERENCES routes(route_id),
track_id INT REFERENCES tracks(track_id),
bounds_n DOUBLE, bounds_s DOUBLE, bounds_e DOUBLE, bounds_w DOUBLE
    12 Key SQL Queries
    Assets in Viewport
-- Tracks in viewport
SELECT track_id, name, difficulty, distance_mi, file_path,
       trailhead_lat, trailhead_lon
FROM tracks
WHERE bounds_w &lt; :east AND bounds_e &gt; :west
  AND bounds_s &lt; :north AND bounds_n &gt; :south
ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20;
-- Routes in viewport
SELECT route_id, name, type, difficulty, distance_mi, file_path,
       trailhead_lat, trailhead_lon
FROM routes
WHERE bounds_w &lt; :east AND bounds_e &gt; :west
  AND bounds_s &lt; :north AND bounds_n &gt; :south
ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20;
-- Trailheads in viewport
SELECT waypoint_id, name, lat, lon, parking_available, facilities
FROM waypoints
WHERE icon_type = 'TRAILHEAD'
  AND lat BETWEEN :south AND :north
  AND lon BETWEEN :west AND :east;
    Unified Asset Search
SELECT 'track' AS type, track_id AS id, name, distance_mi,
       difficulty, bounds_n, bounds_s, bounds_e, bounds_w,
       trailhead_lat AS lat, trailhead_lon AS lon
FROM tracks WHERE name LIKE :query
UNION
SELECT 'route', route_id, name, distance_mi,
       difficulty, bounds_n, bounds_s, bounds_e, bounds_w,
       trailhead_lat, trailhead_lon
FROM routes WHERE name LIKE :query
UNION
SELECT 'trailhead', waypoint_id, name, 0,
       NULL, lat, lat, lon, lon, lat, lon
FROM waypoints WHERE icon_type = 'TRAILHEAD' AND name LIKE :query
UNION
SELECT 'waypoint', waypoint_id, name, 0,
       NULL, lat, lat, lon, lon, lat, lon
FROM waypoints WHERE icon_type != 'TRAILHEAD' AND name LIKE :query
ORDER BY name;
    Rides Departing from Trailhead
-- 0.004 degrees ≈ 0.25 miles proximity threshold
SELECT r.ride_id, r.name, r.ride_date, r.is_public,
       u.first_name, u.last_name
FROM rides r
JOIN users u ON r.organizer_id = u.user_id
WHERE r.trailhead_lat BETWEEN :lat - 0.004 AND :lat + 0.004

var ALL_IDS = ["mapmenu_on", "mapmenu_off", "s01", "s01b", "s02", "s03", "s04", "s05", "s06", "s07", "s08", "s09", "s10", "s10b", "s11", "s12", "s13", "s14", "s15", "s16", "s17", "s18", "s19", "s20", "s20b", "s20c", "s21", "s22", "s23", "s24", "s25", "s26", "s27", "s28", "s29", "s30", "s31", "s32", "s33"];
var currentScreen = null;
function toggleFlow(id) {
    var list = document.getElementById(id);
    var isOpen = list.style.display === "block";
    document.querySelectorAll(".fb").forEach(function(b) { b.classList.remove("open"); });
    document.querySelectorAll(".sl").forEach(function(s) { s.style.display = "none"; });
    if (!isOpen) {
        list.previousElementSibling.classList.add("open");
        list.style.display = "block";
    }
}
function gotoScreen(id, flow, title) {
    currentScreen = id;
    document.querySelectorAll(".si").forEach(function(s) { s.classList.remove("active"); });
    document.querySelectorAll(".si").forEach(function(s) {
        var oc = s.getAttribute("onclick") || "";
        if (oc.indexOf("'" + id + "'") >= 0) s.classList.add("active");
    });
    var main = document.getElementById("main");
    main.innerHTML =
        "" + flow + "" + title + "" +
        "";
    buildScreen(id);
    renderNotes(id);
}
function buildScreen(id) {
    var slot = document.getElementById("phone-slot");
    if (!slot) return;
    var fn = SCREENS[id];
    if (fn) slot.innerHTML = "9:41&#9608;&#9608;&#9608; 100%" + fn() + "";
    else slot.innerHTML = "Screen " + id + " — content coming in next pass";
}
function renderNotes(id) {
    var slot = document.getElementById("notes-slot");
    if (!slot) return;
    var d = SD[id] || {a:[], r:[]};
    var ca = []; try { ca = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("ca_" + id) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
    var cr = []; try { cr = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cr_" + id) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
    var note = ""; try { note = localStorage.getItem("note_" + id) || ""; } catch(e) {}
    var atags = d.a.map(function(f) {
        var sel = ca.indexOf(f) >= 0 ? " sel" : "";
        return "" + f + "";
    }).join("");
    var rtags = d.r.map(function(f) {
        var sel = cr.indexOf(f) >= 0 ? " sel" : "";
        return "" + f + "";
    }).join("");
    slot.innerHTML =
        "" +
        "&#10003; FUNCTIONS ACTIVE &mdash; click to confirm / mark changed" + atags + "" +
        "&#9675; RELATED NOT USED &mdash; click to select for this screen" + rtags + "" +
        "&#9998; SCREEN NOTES &amp; ADJUSTMENT REQUESTS" +
        "" + note + "" +
        "";
}
function toggleTag(id, type, fn) {
    var key = (type === "a" ? "ca_" : "cr_") + id;
    var arr = []; try { arr = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
    var idx = arr.indexOf(fn);
    if (idx >= 0) arr.splice(idx, 1); else arr.push(fn);
    try { localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(arr)); } catch(e) {}
    renderNotes(id);
}
function saveNote(id) {
    try { var el = document.getElementById("note_" + id); if (el) localStorage.setItem("note_" + id, el.value); } catch(e) {}
}
function copyEmail(email) {
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(email).catch(function() {});
    var els = document.querySelectorAll(".email-copy");
    els.forEach(function(el) { if (el.textContent.indexOf(email) >= 0) { el.style.background = "rgba(0,170,68,0.3)"; setTimeout(function() { el.style.background = ""; }, 1200); } });
}
function openExport() {
    var lines = ["GROUPTRACK V3.0 PROTOTYPE REVIEW — " + new Date().toLocaleString(), "=".repeat(55), ""];
    var hasData = false;
    ALL_IDS.forEach(function(id) {
        var note = ""; try { note = localStorage.getItem("note_" + id) || ""; } catch(e) {}
        var ca = []; try { ca = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("ca_" + id) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
        var cr = []; try { cr = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cr_" + id) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
        if (note || ca.length || cr.length) {
            hasData = true;
            lines.push("SCREEN: " + id.toUpperCase());
            if (ca.length) lines.push("  CONFIRMED ACTIVE: " + ca.join(", "));
            if (cr.length) lines.push("  SELECTED FROM RELATED: " + cr.join(", "));
            if (note) lines.push("  NOTES: " + note.trim());
            lines.push("");
        }
    });
    if (!hasData) lines.push("No selections or notes yet.\n\nClick GREEN tags to confirm functions.\nClick GREY tags to add related functions.\nType in notes field.\nThen export and paste to Claude.");
    document.getElementById("export-out").textContent = lines.join("\n");
    document.getElementById("export-modal").classList.add("open");
}
function closeExport() { document.getElementById("export-modal").classList.remove("open"); }
function copyExport() {
    var txt = document.getElementById("export-out").textContent;
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(txt).then(function() {
        var b = document.getElementById("copy-btn");
        b.textContent = "COPIED!"; setTimeout(function() { b.textContent = "COPY ALL"; }, 2000);
    }).catch(function() { document.execCommand("copy"); });
}
function tA(h) {
    var b = h.nextElementSibling, a = h.querySelector("span:last-child");
    if (b.classList.contains("open")) { b.classList.remove("open"); b.style.display = "none"; a.textContent = "▶"; }
    else { b.classList.add("open"); b.style.display = "block"; a.textContent = "▼"; }
}
function bnav(active) {
    var items = [["HOME","&#x1F3E0;","s04","Dashboard"],["RIDES","&#x1F690;","s09","My Rides"],["MAP","&#x1F5FA;","s16","Map - SOLO"],["PROFILE","&#x1F464;","s05","Profile"]];
    return "" + items.map(function(x) {
        return "" +
               "" + x[1] + "" + x[0] + "";
    }).join("") + "";
}
function emailBlock(name, email, phone) {
    var ph = phone ? "&#128222; " + phone + "" : "";
    return "" +
        "" + name + "" +
        "" +
        "&#128203;" + email + "" + ph + "";
}

function mapBase(stateLabel, stateColor, svgContent, hudCols, stopLabel, stopTarget) {
    var hudCells = hudCols.map(function(c) {
        return "" + c[0] + "" + c[1] + "";
    }).join("");
    var stopBtn = "" + stopLabel + "";
    return "" +
        "" + svgContent + "" +
        "" +
        "OFFLINE" +
        "" + stateLabel + "" +
        "SAT" +
        "&#9881;" +
        "" + stopBtn + "" +
        "" + hudCells + "";
}

const SCREENS = 29;
const TITLES = {
  1:'SIGN IN',2:'RIDER TERMS',3:'PRIVACY POLICY',
  4:'DASHBOARD',
  5:'PROFILE',6:'BECOME ORGANIZER',7:'FIELD RADIO',
  8:'MAP SOLO',9:'MAP SETTINGS',10:'MAP CONVOY',11:'MAP ORGANIZED',12:'STOP SURVEY',
  13:'MY RIDES',14:'EXPLORE',15:'CREATE RIDE',16:'RIDE DETAIL',17:'SEND INVITE',18:'BROADCAST',19:'FOLLOWING',20:'INVITE ACCEPT',
  21:'MAP MANAGER',22:'FIND AREA',23:'SET TRAILHEAD',24:'SET MAP AREA',25:'TILE DOWNLOAD',26:'IMPORT ROUTE',27:'OVERLAY SELECTOR',28:'WAYPOINTS',29:'CREATE WAYPOINT'
};
const SECTIONS = {
  1:'A',2:'A',3:'A',
  4:'B',
  5:'C',6:'C',7:'C',
  8:'D',9:'D',10:'D',11:'D',12:'D',
  13:'E',14:'E',15:'E',16:'E',17:'E',18:'E',19:'E',20:'E',
  21:'F',22:'F',23:'F',24:'F',25:'F',26:'F',27:'F',28:'F',29:'F'
};
const SECTION_NAMES = {A:'ONBOARDING',B:'DASHBOARD',C:'ACCOUNT',D:'RIDE MAP',E:'RIDES',F:'MAP MANAGER'};
let current = 1;
function buildSidebar() {
  const sb = document.getElementById('sidebar');
  let lastSec = '';
  for(let i=1;i<=SCREENS;i++){
    const sec = SECTIONS[i];
    if(sec !== lastSec){
      const div = document.createElement('div');
      div.style.cssText='width:36px;font-family:Share Tech Mono,monospace;font-size:8px;color:#F5A623;text-align:center;padding:2px 0;border-top:1px solid rgba(245,166,35,0.3);margin-top:4px;';
      div.textContent=sec;
      sb.appendChild(div);
      lastSec=sec;
    }
    const d = document.createElement('div');
    d.className='sdot'+(i===1?' active':'');
    d.textContent=i;
    d.title=TITLES[i];
    d.onclick=()=>goTo(i);
    sb.appendChild(d);
  }
}
function goTo(n) {
  if(typeof n === 'string') n = parseInt(n);
  if(nSCREENS) return;
  document.getElementById('screen-'+current)?.classList.remove('active');
  document.querySelectorAll('.sdot')[current-1]?.classList.remove('active');
  current=n;
  document.getElementById('screen-'+current)?.classList.add('active');
  document.querySelectorAll('.sdot')[current-1]?.classList.add('active');
  const sec = SECTIONS[current];
  document.getElementById('screenInfo').textContent=
    'SCREEN '+current+' OF '+SCREENS+' — '+SECTION_NAMES[sec]+' — '+TITLES[current];
  window.scrollTo(0,0);
}
function nextScreen(){goTo(current+1);}
function prevScreen(){goTo(current-1);}
function toggleAcc(header){
  const body=header.nextElementSibling;
  const arrow=header.querySelector('.acc-arrow');
  if(body.classList.contains('open')){
    body.classList.remove('open');
    body.style.display='none';
    arrow.textContent='▶';
  } else {
    body.classList.add('open');
    body.style.display='block';
    arrow.textContent='▼';
  }
}
document.addEventListener('keydown',e=>{
  if(e.key==='ArrowRight')nextScreen();
  if(e.key==='ArrowLeft')prevScreen();
});
buildSidebar();

    Our Mission
    Convoy Coordination.Without the Network.
    GroupTrack keeps your group connected when cell service disappears. Built on Meshtastic&#8217;s low-power LoRa mesh radio technology, every rider in your convoy can see every other rider&#8217;s position in real time &#8212; no towers, no data plan, no excuses.
        Whether you&#8217;re leading a UTV convoy through the canyon country of southern Utah, coordinating a group trail ride in the backcountry, or managing search and rescue operations in a dead zone &#8212; GroupTrack gives your group the situational awareness it needs to stay safe, stay together, and stay on track.
        Pre-download your maps. Configure your radios. Head out. GroupTrack does the rest.
          &#128247;
            Real-Time Position
            See every rider on a live map. Updated every few seconds over the mesh.
          &#128225;
            No Cell Required
            Runs entirely on LoRa mesh radio. Works 10+ miles from the nearest tower.
          &#127757;
            Offline Maps
            Pre-download your riding area before you leave. Full map tiles stored on device.
          &#128274;
            Encrypted Mesh
            Private channel with PSK encryption. Only your group sees your group.
    What It Does
    Built for the Trail.
    Every feature in GroupTrack was designed for real-world off-grid use &#8212; by riders, for riders.
        &#128205;
        Live Convoy Map
        See your entire group on an interactive map in real time. Color-coded by rider position in the convoy. Never lose track of who&#8217;s ahead or behind.
        &#127760;
        Offline Map Downloads
        Search for your trail area, draw your download zone, and cache map tiles before you leave. Satellite, topo, hybrid, and road layers all work offline.
        &#128267;
        Mesh Radio Network
        Powered by Meshtastic LoRa radio. Each device acts as a relay, extending range across the entire convoy automatically.
        &#128196;
        Ride Management
        Organizers create rides, set radio configs, and invite riders with a single link. Riders tap the link, download the ride, and go. Zero technical setup required.
        &#127981;
        GPS Track Recording
        Record your ride track with one tap. Pause, resume, and save. Export as KML for Google Earth or share with the group after the ride.
        &#9889;
        One-Boot Radio Config
        Set channel, frequency, PSK, and device settings from the app. Apply with one tap. Radio reboots configured and ready to mesh in under 60 seconds.
    Development Status
    Where We Are Right Now.
        V2.4 — Beta
        GroupTrack V2.4 is live and in the hands of authorized beta testers. The core feature set is proven &#8212; offline maps, live convoy tracking, one-boot radio configuration, and GPS track recording all working on Android in the field.V3.0 brings the full ride management platform including Google Sign-In, cloud-based ride creation, and invite link distribution.

GroupTrack
Version 2.5 Release Notes — What&rsquo;s New
Field Test Release &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; Map Feature Update &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; updated 2026-06-02
About this release
V2.5 completes the free map product: trail and trailhead data you can download straight onto your maps, plus a single, consistent way to show and hide Trails, Tracks, Waypoints, and Routes on both the Convoy Map and the Planning Map. This is a FIELD TEST build — known rough edges are listed at the end.
New in this build (2026-06-02): Track import fixed for large files
  Big GPX files import without crashing. Large onX &ldquo;markups&rdquo; exports (25MB+, dozens of tracks) used to crash the app during import — that&rsquo;s fixed. You can import your full track collection in one pass.
  Much faster. Large tracks that took minutes each now take seconds.
  Import summary. After an import you see &ldquo;X new / Y already in library&rdquo; — how many tracks were actually added versus already on your device.
  Safe to re-import. Tracks already saved are recognized by their shape and skipped — re-importing the same file does not create duplicates.
  Limitation this build: importing a GPX brings in its tracks only. Any waypoints or routes in the file are skipped for now (a separate import feature is coming). Dropping waypoints on the map yourself still works.
Headline: Import Utah Trails onto your map
The trail source catalog lets you pull a full set of Utah trails and trailhead waypoints directly onto your maps as artifacts — no files to copy, and no internet needed once they&rsquo;re down.
How to import UGRC Utah Trails:
  Open Work with Artifacts (accordion button).
  Select Import Trails. The trail source list displays.
  Select UGRC Utah Trails.
  Tap Validate/Confirm. Trails and trailhead waypoints download as artifacts.
  Fully close the app, force close, then reopen. Imported trails and trailheads now appear.
If imported trails don&rsquo;t show: (1) Fully close and reopen (or Force Stop) so trail data loads. (2) Zoom in — about 49,000 trails only draw at close zoom (see Known Issues).
What else is new
  Trail source catalog — browse and import. UGRC Utah Trails first (~49,000 trails + 591 trailheads). BLM/USFS planned.
  One consistent artifact display — Trails/Tracks/Waypoints/Routes show and hide the same way on both maps.
  Independent map selections — the Convoy and Planning maps each keep their own selections, saved across restarts.
  SELECTED shows exactly what you pick — draws only the items you checked, consistent on both maps.
  Drop waypoints on the map — long-press empty ground for a 12-type picker plus an optional name. (Works on the Planning Map; Convoy Map waypoint drop is in progress — see Known Issues.)
  Work with Artifacts panel — accordion; per-type OFF / ON / SELECTED plus an item list.
  Default on launch — Trails ON, others OFF.
  RESYNC TRACKS — rebuilds the track list from your saved GPX files, and adds any track on the device that isn&rsquo;t yet in the database.
  Zoom readout — the compass shows the zoom level (N &middot; Z##).
  Standalone GPS / offline maps — carried from V2.4.
Requirements
Android 8.0+ (tablet recommended). Auto-update via the Play Store internal track. 500MB+ free for tiles (trail data ~15–30MB per state). Meshtastic SenseCAP T1000-E or LoRa firmware 2.6+ (for convoy only, not maps). Internet needed once to import/download.
Known issues — please read
  Trails not visible zoomed far out — expected; zoom in.
  Item list sometimes shows no names — known; being addressed.
  Item list shows up to 200 entries — paging is coming in a later build.
  After a track import, the artifact list may not refresh until you leave the screen and return. (Tracks appear on the map right away.)
  Convoy Map: QUEUES button and waypoint long-press are not working yet — both work on the Planning Map; convoy parity is in progress.
  Tracks missing after an update — RESYNC TRACKS rebuilds.
Resolved since last build
  Track re-import no longer duplicates. The earlier &ldquo;don&rsquo;t import the same tracks repeatedly&rdquo; warning is fixed for tracks — they&rsquo;re de-duplicated by shape, so re-importing skips ones already present. (Trail-source re-import dedupe is still rolling out — import UGRC once.)
  Large track files no longer crash the import.
  Map selections are independent per map and saved.
Troubleshooting
  Imported trails don&rsquo;t appear &rarr; zoom in; confirm the import finished.
  Imported tracks don&rsquo;t appear in the list &rarr; leave the screen and return; they&rsquo;re already on the map.
  A big track file used to crash &rarr; fixed in this build; if any import still stalls, note the file size and track count and report it.
  No vehicles (convoy) &rarr; is the radio connected (green)? Same channel and PSK?
  Tiles blank offline &rarr; download tiles while online first.
  Tiles not loading online &rarr; check your internet.
  A track is missing &rarr; RESYNC TRACKS.
  Anything else &rarr; report it (note what you tapped and what you expected).
